text:
We consider the design of experiments to evaluate treatments that are
administered by self-interested agents, each seeking to achieve the highest
evaluation and win the experiment. For example, in an advertising experiment, a
company wishes to evaluate two marketing agents in terms of their efficacy in
viral marketing, and assign a contract to the winner agent. Contrary to
traditional experimental design, this problem has two new implications. First,
the experiment induces a game among agents, where each agent can select from
multiple versions of the treatment it administers. Second, the action of one
agent -- selection of treatment version -- may affect the actions of another
agent, with the resulting strategic interference complicating the evaluation of
agents. An incentive-compatible experiment design is one with an equilibrium
where each agent selects its natural action, which is the action that would
maximize the performance of the agent if there was no competition (e.g.,
expected number of conversions if agent was assigned the contract). Under a
general formulation of experimental design, we identify sufficient conditions
that guarantee incentive-compatible experiments. These conditions rely on the
existence of statistics that can estimate how agents would perform without
competition, and their use in constructing score functions to evaluate the
agents. In the setting with no strategic interference, we also study the power
of the design, i.e., the probability that the best agent wins, and show how to
improve the power of incentive-compatible designs. From the technical side, our
theory uses a range of statistical methods such as hypothesis testing,
variance-stabilizing transformations and the Delta method, all of which rely on
asymptotics.
label: human

text:
We present the Multifrequency Snapshot Sky Survey (MSSS), the first
northern-sky LOFAR imaging survey. In this introductory paper, we first
describe in detail the motivation and design of the survey. Compared to
previous radio surveys, MSSS is exceptional due to its intrinsic multifrequency
nature providing information about the spectral properties of the detected
sources over more than two octaves (from 30 to 160 MHz). The broadband
frequency coverage, together with the fast survey speed generated by LOFAR's
multibeaming capabilities, make MSSS the first survey of the sort anticipated
to be carried out with the forthcoming Square Kilometre Array (SKA). Two of the
sixteen frequency bands included in the survey were chosen to exactly overlap
the frequency coverage of large-area Very Large Array (VLA) and Giant Metrewave
Radio Telescope (GMRT) surveys at 74 MHz and 151 MHz respectively. The survey
performance is illustrated within the "MSSS Verification Field" (MVF), a region
of 100 square degrees centered at J2000 (RA,Dec)=(15h,69deg). The MSSS results
from the MVF are compared with previous radio survey catalogs. We assess the
flux and astrometric uncertainties in the catalog, as well as the completeness
and reliability considering our source finding strategy. We determine the 90%
completeness levels within the MVF to be 100 mJy at 135 MHz with 108"
resolution, and 550 mJy at 50 MHz with 166" resolution. Images and catalogs for
the full survey, expected to contain 150,000-200,000 sources, will be released
to a public web server. We outline the plans for the ongoing production of the
final survey products, and the ultimate public release of images and source
catalogs.
label: human

text: In the study we conducted on the competition between spin fluctuations in Ca$_{2-x}$Sr$_{x}$RuO$_{4}$ around $x=0.5, we investigated the intricate interplay between the various magnetic phases in this compound. Our research aimed to elucidate the predominant spin fluctuations near the critical doping level of x=0.5 in order to understand the unconventional behavior observed in the material. Through a combination of theoretical analysis and experimental measurements, we uncovered a complex scenario where the spin fluctuations manifesting in the system compete for dominance. By examining the temperature-dependent behaviors of these spin fluctuations, we were able to characterize their distinct roles and interactions within the material.  Our results reveal a delicate balance between different types of spin fluctuations near the critical doping level of x=0.5, shedding light on the underlying mechanisms driving the magnetic properties of Ca$_{2-x}$Sr$_{x}$RuO$_{4}$. The findings from this study provide valuable insights into the nature of magnetic phases in this compound and contribute to the broader understanding of correlated electron systems. Our methodology involved a combination of theoretical modeling and experimental techniques, providing a comprehensive analysis of the competition between spin fluctuations in this intriguing material.
label: machine

text:
A hybrid asymptotic-numerical method is presented for obtaining the full
probability distribution of capture times of a random walker by multiple small
traps located inside a bounded two-dimensional domain with reflective
boundaries. As motivation for this study, we calculate the variance in the
capture time of a random walker by a single interior trap and determine this
quantity to be comparable in magnitude to the mean. This implies that the mean
is not necessarily reflective of typical capture times and that the full
density must be determined. To solve the underlying diffusion equation, the
method of Laplace transforms is used to obtain an elliptic problem of modified
Helmholtz type. In the limit of vanishing trap sizes, each trap is represented
as a Dirac point source which permits the solution of the transform equation to
be represented as a superposition of Helmholtz Green's functions. Using this
solution, we construct asymptotic short time solutions of the first passage
time density which captures peaks associated with rapid capture by the
absorbing traps. When numerical evaluation of the Helmholtz Green's function is
employed followed by numerical inversion of the Laplace transform, the method
reproduces the density for larger times. We demonstrate the accuracy of our
solution technique with comparison to statistics obtained from a time-dependent
solution of the diffusion equation and discrete particle simulations. In
particular, we demonstrate that the method is capable of capturing the
multimodal behavior in the capture time density that arises when the traps are
strategically arranged. The hybrid method presented can be applied to scenarios
involving both arbitrary domains and trap shapes.
label: human

text:
We have used optical observations of resolved stars from the Panchromatic
Hubble Andromeda Treasury (PHAT) to measure the recent (< 500 Myr) star
formation histories (SFHs) of 33 FUV-bright regions in M31. The region areas
ranged from ~$10^4$ to $10^6$ pc$^2$, which allowed us to test the reliability
of FUV flux as a tracer of recent star formation on sub-kpc scales. The star
formation rates (SFRs) derived from the extinction-corrected observed FUV
fluxes were, on average, consistent with the 100-Myr mean SFRs of the SFHs to
within the 1$\sigma$ scatter. Overall, the scatter was larger than the
uncertainties in the SFRs and particularly evident among the smallest regions.
The scatter was consistent with an even combination of discrete sampling of the
initial mass function and high variability in the SFHs. This result
demonstrates the importance of satisfying both the full-IMF and the
constant-SFR assumptions for obtaining precise SFR estimates from FUV flux.
Assuming a robust FUV extinction correction, we estimate that a factor of 2.5
uncertainty can be expected in FUV-based SFRs for regions smaller than $10^5$
pc$^2$, or a few hundred pc. We also examined ages and masses derived from UV
flux under the common assumption that the regions are simple stellar
populations (SSPs). The SFHs showed that most of the regions are not SSPs, and
the age and mass estimates were correspondingly discrepant from the SFHs. For
those regions with SSP-like SFHs, we found mean discrepancies of 10 Myr in age
and a factor of 3 to 4 in mass. It was not possible to distinguish the SSP-like
regions from the others based on integrated FUV flux.
label: human

text: In our recent study, we explored the operational limits of electroluminescent (EL) time-projection chambers (TPCs) at the thermal diffusion limit. EL-TPCs, a promising alternative to traditional gas-filled TPCs, have shown great potential in enhancing particle identification capabilities and increasing overall detection efficiency. However, the thermal diffusion of electrons in EL materials constitutes a significant challenge in achieving optimal TPC performance at high voltages.  We employed a custom-designed EL sensor, with dimensions of 6 cm × 6 cm, incorporating poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA) as the EL material, sandwiched between copper electrodes. To assess the thermal diffusion effects, we applied varying voltages up to 30 kV to the EL sensor while measuring the charge collection efficiency and the charge distribution profile of EL signals. The experiments were carried out in a vacuum environment at room temperature.  Our findings indicated that at voltages beyond the thermal diffusion limit (approximately 15 kV for our EL sensor), charge carriers started to recombine, resulting in a reduced charge collection efficiency and significant distortions in the charge distribution profile. These distortions introduced errors in the position measurement and reduced the overall detection efficiency of the EL-TPC.  To mitigate the effects of thermal diffusion at high voltages, we propose implementing several possible solutions, including the use of thin EL layers, reducing the size of the EL pixels, employing cooling systems, and optimizing the electrode geometry. The proposed solutions can potentially extend the operational limits of EL-TPCs, making them more suitable for applications that require higher voltage and larger detection areas.  Our work not only sheds light on the thermal diffusion limit of EL-TPCs but also provides valuable insights into the practical considerations and potential optimizations for future EL sensor designs. This study significantly advances the understanding of EL materials' limitations and paves the way for developing improved EL-TPCs with enhanced performance.
label: machine

text: Nonperturbative resonant strong field ionization (NRSFI) of atomic hydrogen is a significant phenomenon in strong field physics, where an atom is ionized by a resonant, intense laser field, without the influence of perturbations from lower field states. In this study, we explore the underlying mechanisms of NRSFI through a combination of theoretical analysis and experimental measurements.  First, we provide a brief overview of the relevant theoretical background, including the Keldysh-Faisal condition and the strong field approximation. We then present the key assumptions of the NRSFI model, which is based on the three-step model for ionization and the resonant condition for laser-atom interaction. These assumptions enable us to understand the mechanism of NRSFI as a quantum mechanical tunneling process.  Our experimental investigations employ a high-intensity femtosecond laser system to generate the required resonant laser fields. By measuring the photoelectron angular distributions and kinetic energies under various laser parameters, we confirm the existence of NRSFI in atomic hydrogen.  Furthermore, we analyze the dependence of the NRSFI efficiency on the laser intensity, detuning, and polarization. Our results demonstrate that the NRSFI process is most efficient under highly resonant conditions, with the laser pulse intensity close to the critical value, and with linearly polarized laser fields.  Finally, we discuss the implications of our findings on future applications of nonperturbative resonant strong field ionization in areas such as high harmonic generation, extreme ultraviolet (XUV) photolithography, and X-ray free electron lasers. In conclusion, this research sheds light on the fundamental aspects of strong field ionization and provides valuable insights into the nonperturbative resonant strong field ionization mechanism of atomic hydrogen.
label: machine

text:
Gravitational redshift as a relativistic effect in cosmological objects is
investigated. Possible signatures of the gravitational redshift in measurements
of satellite galaxies in clusters of galaxies, intracluster gas, as well as
galaxies associated with voids are investigated by developing simple
theoretical models. In the analysis of the gravitational redshift of satellite
galaxies, we develop a very simple analytic model for satellite galaxies
virialised in halos, which enables us to evaluate the signals depending on the
properties of the halo occupation distribution of galaxies. We obtain results
consistent with recent previous results, though our results are restricted to
the satellite galaxies inside the virial radius. In the analysis of
intracluster gas, we develop a simple analytic model including the effect of
random motions of gases, which are assumed to generate nonthermal pressure. We
demonstrate a possible contribution of the random motions of gases to the
gravitational redshift. We also investigate a possible signature of the
gravitational redshift in measurements of galaxies associated with voids, for
the first time as far as we know, by utilising a simple analytic model. We show
that the second-order Hubble term, which appears in the expansion of the scale
factor around the centre of a void, may make a significant contribution
depending on the way the galaxy samples are analysed.
label: human

text:
Supernova (SN) explosions deposit prodigious energy and momentum in their
environments, with the former regulating multiphase thermal structure and the
latter regulating turbulence and star formation rates in the interstellar
medium (ISM). However, systematic studies quantifying the impact of SNe in
realistic inhomogeneous ISM conditions have been lacking. Using
three-dimensional hydrodynamic simulations, we investigate the dependence of
radial momentum injection on both physical conditions (considering a range of
mean density n=0.1-100) and numerical parameters. Our inhomogeneous simulations
adopt two-phase background states that result from thermal instability in
atomic gas. Although the SNR morphology becomes highly complex for
inhomogeneous backgrounds, the radial momentum injection is remarkably
insensitive to environmental details. For our two-phase simulations, the final
momentum produced by a single SN is given by 2.8*10^5 M_sun*km/s n^{-0.17}.
This is only 5% less than the momentum injection for a homogeneous environment
with the same mean density, and only 30% greater than the momentum at the time
of shell formation. The maximum mass in hot gas is quite insensitive to
environmental inhomogeneity. Strong magnetic fields alter the hot gas mass at
very late times, but the momentum injection remains the same. Initial
experiments with multiple spatially-correlated SNe show a momentum per event
nearly as large as single-SN cases. We also present a full numerical parameter
study to assess convergence requirements. For convergence in the momentum and
other quantities, we find that the numerical resolution dx and the initial size
of the SNR r_init must satisfy dx, r_init<r_sf/3, where the shell formation
radius is given by r_sf = 30 pc n^{-0.46} for two-phase models (or 30% smaller
for a homogeneous medium).
label: human

text:
We study the evolution of planetesimals in evolved gaseous disks, which orbit
a solar-mass star and harbor a Jupiter-mass planet at a_p~5AU. The gas dynamics
is modeled with a three-dimensional hydrodynamics code that employes
nested-grids and achieves a resolution of one Jupiter's radius in the
circumplanetary disk. The code models solids as individual particles.
Planetesimals are subjected to gravitational forces by the star and the planet,
drag force by the gas, disruption via ram pressure, and mass loss through
ablation. The mass evolution of solids is calculated self-consistently with
their temperature, velocity, and position. We consider icy and icy/rocky bodies
of radius 0.1-100km, initially deployed on orbits around the star within a few
Hill radii (Rhill) of the planet's orbit. Planetesimals are scattered inward,
outward, and toward disk regions of radius r>>a_p. Scattering can relocate
significant amounts of solids, provided that regions |r-a_p|~ 3Rhill are
replenished with planetesimals. Scattered bodies can be temporarily captured on
planetocentric orbits. Ablation consumes nearly all solids at gas temperatures
> ~220K. Super-keplerian rotation around and beyond the outer edge of the gas
gap can segregate < ~0.1km bodies, producing solid gap edges at size-dependent
radial locations. Capture, break-up, and ablation of solids result in a
dust-laden circumplanetary disk with low surface densities of km-size
planetesimals, implying relatively long timescales for satellite formation.
After a giant planet acquires most of its mass, accretion of solids is unlikely
to alter significantly its heavy-element content. The luminosity generated by
solids' accretion can be of a similar order of magnitude to the contraction
luminosity.
label: human

text:
The training of machine learning models is typically carried out using some
form of gradient descent, often with great success. However, non-asymptotic
analyses of first-order optimization algorithms typically employ a gradient
smoothness assumption (formally, Lipschitz continuity of the gradient) that is
too strong to be applicable in the case of deep neural networks. To address
this, we propose an algorithm named duality structure gradient descent (DSGD)
that is amenable to non-asymptotic performance analysis, under mild assumptions
on the training set and network architecture. The algorithm can be viewed as a
form of layer-wise coordinate descent, where at each iteration the algorithm
chooses one layer of the network to update. The decision of what layer to
update is done in a greedy fashion, based on a rigorous lower bound on the
improvement of the objective function for each choice of layer. In the
analysis, we bound the time required to reach approximate stationary points, in
both the deterministic and stochastic settings. The convergence is measured in
terms of a parameter-dependent family of norms that is derived from the network
architecture and designed to confirm a smoothness-like property on the gradient
of the training loss function. We empirically demonstrate the behavior of DSGD
in several neural network training scenarios.
label: human

text:
The Universe is mostly composed of large and relatively empty domains known
as cosmic voids, whereas its matter content is predominantly distributed along
their boundaries. The remaining material inside them, either dark or luminous
matter, is attracted to these boundaries and causes voids to expand faster and
to grow emptier over time. Using the distribution of galaxies centered on voids
identified in the Sloan Digital Sky Survey and adopting minimal assumptions on
the statistical motion of these galaxies, we constrain the average matter
content $\Omega_\mathrm{m}=0.281\pm0.031$ in the Universe today, as well as the
linear growth rate of structure $f/b=0.417\pm0.089$ at median redshift
$\bar{z}=0.57$, where $b$ is the galaxy bias ($68\%$ C.L.). These values
originate from a percent-level measurement of the anisotropic distortion in the
void-galaxy cross-correlation function, $\varepsilon = 1.003\pm0.012$, and are
robust to consistency tests with bootstraps of the data and simulated mock
catalogs within an additional systematic uncertainty of half that size. They
surpass (and are complementary to) existing constraints by unlocking
cosmological information on smaller scales through an accurate model of
nonlinear clustering and dynamics in void environments. As such, our analysis
furnishes a powerful probe of deviations from Einstein's general relativity in
the low-density regime which has largely remained untested so far. We find no
evidence for such deviations in the data at hand.
label: human

text:
We derive a sum rule which shows that the Froissart-Martin bound for the
asymptotic behaviour of the $\pi\pi$ total cross sections at high energies, if
modulated by the Lukaszuk-Martin coefficient of the leading $\log^2 s$
behaviour, cannot be an optimal bound in QCD. We next compute the total cross
sections for $\pi^+ \pi^-$, $\pi^{\pm} \pi^0$ and $\pi^0 \pi^0$ scattering
within the framework of the constituent chiral quark model (C$\chi$QM) in the
limit of a large number of colours $\Nc$ and discuss their asymptotic
behaviours. The same $\pi\pi$ cross sections are also discussed within the
general framework of Large-\Nc~QCD and we show that it is possible to make an
Ansatz for the isospin $I=1$ and $I=0$ spectrum which satisfy the
Froissart-Martin bound with coefficients which, contrary to the Lukaszuk-Martin
coefficient, are not singular in the chiral limit and have the correct
Large-\Nc~counting. We finally propose a simple phenomenological model which
matches the low energy behaviours of the $\sigma_{\pi^{\pm}\pi^0}^{\rm
total}(s)$ cross section predicted by the C$\chi$QM with the high energy
behaviour predicted by the Large-$\Nc$ Ansatz. The magnitude of these cross
sections at very high energies is of the order of those observed for the $pp$
and $p{\bar p}$ scattering total cross sections.
label: human

text: Vacuum Cherenkov radiation phenomena for Lorentz-violating fermions in the context of Lorentz symmetry breaking are examined in this study. The main objective is to investigate the potential emission of Cherenkov radiation in the absence of material medium due to Lorentz violation in fermionic systems. The methodology involves theoretical calculations within the framework of Standard Model Extension (SME) to analyze the Cherenkov radiation effects caused by Lorentz violation in fermions. Key findings suggest that Lorentz-violating fermions can indeed exhibit vacuum Cherenkov radiation under specific conditions, which could have implications for high-energy physics and Lorentz symmetry studies. The study highlights the importance of considering Lorentz violation in fermionic systems when studying Cherenkov radiation, opening up new avenues for experimental verification and theoretical exploration in the field. In conclusion, the research contributes to the broader understanding of vacuum Cherenkov radiation phenomena in the presence of Lorentz symmetry breaking in fermionic systems, shedding light on the intricate interplay between fundamental symmetries and high-energy phenomena.
label: machine

text:
Motivated by the sequence form formulation of Koller et al. (GEB'96), this
paper defines {\em bilinear games}, and proposes efficient algorithms for its
rank based subclasses. Bilinear games are two-player non-cooperative
single-shot games with compact polytopal strategy sets and two payoff matrices
(A,B) such that when (x,y) is the played strategy profile, the payoffs of the
players are xAy and xBy respectively. We show that bilinear games are very
general and capture many interesting classes of games like bimatrix games, two
player Bayesian games, polymatrix games, two-player extensive form games with
perfect recall etc. as special cases, and hence are hard to solve in general.
  Existence of a (symmetric) Nash equilibrium for (symmetric) bilinear games
follow directly from the known results. For a given bilinear game, we define
its {\em Best Response Polytopes} (BRPs) and characterize the set of Nash
equilibria as {\em fully-labeled} pairs in the BRPs. We consider a rank based
hierarchy of bilinear games, where rank of a game (A,B) is defined as
rank(A+B). In this paper, we give polynomial time algorithms to compute Nash
equilibrium for special classes of bilinear games:
  (i) Rank-1 games (i.e., rank(A+B)=1). (ii) FPTAS for constant rank games
(i.e., rank(A+B) is constant). (iii) When rank(A) or rank(B) is constant. This
improves the results by Lipton et al. (EC'03) and Kannan et al. (ET'09), for
bimatrix games with low rank matrices.
label: human

text: In recent years, the study of solitons has garnered significant attention due to their implications in various physical systems, particularly in the context of Lorentz and CPT (Charge, Parity, Time) breaking phenomena. This research analyzes the information-entropy properties of traveling solitons within these systems to understand how symmetries influence soliton dynamics. The objective of this study is to establish a theoretical framework that correlates the information content of solitons with the breaking of Lorentz and CPT symmetries.   We employed a combination of analytical and numerical techniques to derive the soliton solutions under different symmetry-breaking conditions. The information entropy was calculated using statistical mechanics principles, offering a quantitative measure of disorder and complexity within the traveling solitons.   Key findings indicate that the breaking of Lorentz and CPT symmetries alters the stability and propagation characteristics of solitons significantly. Specifically, we demonstrated that higher information entropy corresponds to increased sensitivity to perturbations, suggesting that solitons in Lorentz and CPT breaking systems exhibit richer dynamical behavior.   In conclusion, the insights gained from this study underscore the profound effects of symmetry breaking on soliton dynamics, as evidenced by their information-entropy characteristics. This research not only contributes to the theoretical understanding of solitons in fundamental physics but also opens avenues for exploring their applications in advanced materials and wave phenomena.
label: machine

text:
Recent observations suggest ongoing planet formation in the innermost parsec
of the Galactic center (GC). The super-massive black hole (SMBH) might strip
planets or planetary embryos from their parent star, bringing them close enough
to be tidally disrupted. Photoevaporation by the ultraviolet field of young
stars, combined with ongoing tidal disruption, could enhance the near-infrared
luminosity of such starless planets, making their detection possible even with
current facilities. In this paper, we investigate the chance of planet tidal
captures by means of high-accuracy N-body simulations exploiting Mikkola's
algorithmic regularization. We consider both planets lying in the clockwise
(CW) disk and planets initially bound to the S-stars. We show that tidally
captured planets remain on orbits close to those of their parent star.
Moreover, the semi-major axis of the planet orbit can be predicted by simple
analytic assumptions in the case of prograde orbits. We find that starless
planets that were initially bound to CW disk stars have mild eccentricities and
tend to remain in the CW disk. However, we speculate that angular momentum
diffusion and scattering with other young stars in the CW disk might bring
starless planets on low-angular momentum orbits. In contrast, planets initially
bound to S-stars are captured by the SMBH on highly eccentric orbits, matching
the orbital properties of the G1 and G2 clouds. Our predictions apply not only
to planets but also to low-mass stars initially bound to the S-stars and
tidally captured by the SMBH.
label: human

text: This study presents a comprehensive investigation of the isolated galaxy CIG 340 (IC 2487), focusing on its 12 kiloparsec (kpc) H I (hydrogen) extension and other associated H I asymmetries. Located in the Local Group, CIG 340 is a relatively unobscured galaxy with a high H I content, making it an ideal target for exploring the interplay between H I distribution, gas dynamics, and galaxy evolution.  The objective of this research is to investigate the physical mechanisms underlying the observed H I extension and asymmetries in CIG 340, shedding light on the galaxy's internal dynamics and interactions with its environment. A combination of high-resolution H I observations from the Arecibo Legacy Fast Radio Burst (ALFREDO) survey and archival data from the H I Parkes All-Sky Survey (HIPASS) were used to create a detailed map of the galaxy's H I distribution.  Our analysis reveals a complex H I morphology, characterized by a 12 kpc extension along the galaxy's major axis, which is offset by approximately 2 kpc from the galaxy's center. Additionally, we detect significant H I asymmetries in the galaxy's disk, suggesting a dynamic and evolving H I distribution. Our findings indicate that the observed H I extension and asymmetries are likely the result of a combination of internal and external factors, including galaxy-scale gas flows, tidal interactions, and feedback mechanisms. Overall, this study provides new insights into the H I dynamics of isolated galaxies, highlighting the importance of considering the interplay between gas and galaxy evolution in the context of galaxy-scale interactions.
label: machine

text:
In this paper, we present all constant solutions of the Yang-Mills equations
with ${\rm SU}(2)$ gauge symmetry for an arbitrary constant non-Abelian current
in Euclidean space ${\mathbb R}^n$ of arbitrary finite dimension $n$. Using the
invariance of the Yang-Mills equations under the orthogonal transformations of
coordinates and gauge invariance, we choose a specific system of coordinates
and a specific gauge fixing for each constant current and obtain all constant
solutions of the Yang-Mills equations in this system of coordinates with this
gauge fixing, and then in the original system of coordinates with the original
gauge fixing. We use the singular value decomposition method and the method of
two-sheeted covering of orthogonal group by spin group to do this. We prove
that the number (0, 1, or 2) of constant solutions of the Yang-Mills equations
in terms of the strength of the Yang-Mills field depends on the singular values
of the matrix of current. The explicit form of all solutions and the invariant
$F^2$ can always be written using singular values of this matrix. The relevance
of the study is explained by the fact that the Yang-Mills equations describe
electroweak interactions in the case of the Lie group ${\rm SU}(2)$.
Nonconstant solutions of the Yang-Mills equations can be considered in the form
of series of perturbation theory. The results of this paper are new and can be
used to solve some problems in particle physics, in particular, to describe
physical vacuum and to fully understand a quantum gauge theory.
label: human

text:
One of the central issues in the debate on network neutrality has been
whether one should allow or prevent preferential treatment by an internet
service provider (ISP) of traffic according to its origin. This raised the
question of whether to allow an ISP to have exclusive agreement with a content
provider (CP). In this paper we consider discrimination in the opposite
direction. We study the impact that a CP can have on the benefits of several
competing ISPs by sharing private information concerning the demand for its
content. More precisely, we consider ISPs that compete over access to one
common CP. Each ISP selects the price that it charges its subscribers for
accessing the content. The CP is assumed to have private information about
demand for its content, and in particular, about the inverse demand function
corresponding to the content. The competing ISPs are assumed to have knowledge
on only the statistical distribution of these functions. We derive in this
paper models for studying the impact that the CP can have on the utilities of
the ISPs by favoring one of them by exclusively revealing its private
information. We also consider the case where CP can charge ISPs for providing
such information. We propose two mechanisms based on {\em weighted proportional
fairness} for payment between ISPs and CP. Finally, we compare the social
utility resulting from these mechanisms with the optimal social utility by
introducing a performance metric termed as {\em price of partial bargaining}
label: human

text: The study of stochastic differential equations (SDEs) associated with the Burgers equation is crucial for understanding the behavior of nonlinear systems influenced by randomness. The unbounded gradients often encountered in such equations pose significant challenges in both theoretical analysis and numerical simulations. This research addresses the suppression of these unbounded gradients, which are typically manifested in the solutions of SDEs associated with the Burgers equation. The primary objective is to investigate methods that effectively control the growth of these gradients, thus maintaining solution integrity and enhancing computational tractability. The methodology involves the application of regularization techniques, coupled with adaptive stochastic calculus, to manage gradient escalation. Specifically, a combination of viscosity solutions and noise perturbations is employed to stabilize the solution space. Our key findings demonstrate that implementing these techniques significantly suppresses the unbounded gradients, resulting in bounded solutions with improved stability and accuracy. Additionally, numerical experiments confirm the effectiveness of our proposed approach, as the modified SDE exhibits better convergence properties and reduced computational errors compared to traditional methods. In conclusion, the study offers a robust framework for managing unbounded gradients in stochastic Burgers equations, advancing both theoretical understanding and practical application in complex systems. These findings contribute to the broader field of stochastic analysis by providing insights into gradient suppression techniques, paving the way for future research in the stabilization of nonlinear stochastic systems.
label: machine

text: Extreme weather events, such as hurricanes, floods, and heatwaves, pose significant challenges to communities and ecosystems worldwide. This research aims to develop a comprehensive large-scale climate dataset to facilitate semi-supervised detection, localization, and understanding of these events. The methodology involves the integration of satellite imagery, weather station data, and socio-economic indicators to create a multi-dimensional dataset. We employed advanced machine learning techniques, specifically semi-supervised learning algorithms, to analyze and classify extreme weather patterns, leveraging both labeled and unlabeled data for improved predictive accuracy. Key findings indicate that the semi-supervised approach significantly enhances the detection capabilities of extreme weather events, achieving a classification accuracy of over 85%. Furthermore, the localization accuracy reached 90%, demonstrating the effectiveness of the dataset in pinpointing affected regions. The analysis revealed discernible trends in the frequency and intensity of extreme events, correlating them with climate change indicators and urbanization patterns. In conclusion, this research provides a valuable resource for researchers and policymakers in understanding the dynamics of extreme weather events. Our dataset not only aids in the timely detection and localization of such events but also contributes to the broader discourse on climate change adaptation and mitigation strategies. This work highlights the necessity for continued investment in climate data infrastructure and analytics to enhance resilience against extreme weather conditions.
label: machine

text:
With the explosive growth of web-based cameras and mobile devices, billions
of photographs are uploaded to the internet. We can trivially collect a huge
number of photo streams for various goals, such as image clustering, 3D scene
reconstruction, and other big data applications. However, such tasks are not
easy due to the fact the retrieved photos can have large variations in their
view perspectives, resolutions, lighting, noises, and distortions.
Fur-thermore, with the occlusion of unexpected objects like people, vehicles,
it is even more challenging to find feature correspondences and reconstruct
re-alistic scenes. In this paper, we propose a structure-based image completion
algorithm for object removal that produces visually plausible content with
consistent structure and scene texture. We use an edge matching technique to
infer the potential structure of the unknown region. Driven by the estimated
structure, texture synthesis is performed automatically along the estimated
curves. We evaluate the proposed method on different types of images: from
highly structured indoor environment to natural scenes. Our experimental
results demonstrate satisfactory performance that can be potentially used for
subsequent big data processing, such as image localization, object retrieval,
and scene reconstruction. Our experiments show that this approach achieves
favorable results that outperform existing state-of-the-art techniques.
label: human

text:
With the increase of huge amounts of data in volume, velocity, and variety,
the need for capacity of Redundant Arrays of Inexpensive Disks (RAID) storage
systems is dramatically growing. However, the probability of disk failures in
RAID storage systems is sharply high with the increase of program/erase cycles,
read cycles, and retention time. Furthermore, they are faced with more
challenges in fault tolerance, storage efficiency, computational complexity,
and expandability. This article presents a novel data layout scheme for RAID
storage System using Random Binary Extensive Code (RBEC), which are designed to
ensure random expandability, high reliability, and availability of data in RAID
storage systems. RBEC is a family of systematic code, in which the generator
matrix consists of two submatrices with entries over GF(2), an identity matrix
on the top, and another submatrix on the bottom. Compared with the existed
approaches, the attractive advantages of our schemes include 1) they are
completely implemented based on only simple eXclusive OR (XOR) operations and
have systematic code property, 2) they can provide arbitrary fault tolerance,
3) their storage efficiency is quasi-optimal, and 4) data and parity disks of
RAID storage systems can be randomly expanded according to practical
requirements. Thus, our scheme is particularly suitable for RAID storage
systems that need higher reliability, availability, and expandability.

text: We report the successful implementation of laser cooling by collisional redistribution of radiation (LCCRR) using a diode-pumped NdYAG laser and a cesium vapor cell. LCCRR is a novel cooling mechanism that utilizes the energy transfer between lasers and collisional redistribution of radiation among atoms to achieve cooling. In contrast to traditional methods, such as Doppler and Sisyphus cooling, which rely on the interaction between lasers and individual atoms, LCCRR functions through the collective interaction between the laser radiation field and the entire atomic ensemble.  Our experimental setup consisted of a 1064 nm NdYAG laser and a cesium vapor cell with a magnetic field gradient. We employed a high-finesse optical cavity to enhance the optical power within the cell, ensuring the maximum optical density required for LCCRR. The cesium vapor was prepared through an optical molasses technique, which provided a thermal velocity distribution for the atoms. To observe the cooling effect, we measured the temperature and density of the atomic cloud using absorption imaging and time-of-flight techniques.  Our results showed a significant decrease in temperature and an increase in density, reaching 331 nK and 2.3 x 10^13 atoms/cm^3, respectively. We observed a 30% decrease in temperature compared to an unmagnetized cesium vapor cell, demonstrating the effectiveness of LCCRR. We attribute this cooling mechanism to the collisional redistribution of radiation, which allows for efficient energy transfer between excited and unexcited atoms, resulting in a cooled atomic ensemble.  In conclusion, we have demonstrated the successful implementation of laser cooling by collisional redistribution of radiation using a diode-pumped NdYAG laser and a cesium vapor cell. Our findings show that LCCRR is an effective cooling mechanism that differs from traditional methods by relying on the collective interaction between the laser radiation field and the entire atomic ensemble. The presented experimental results pave the way for further investigations in this novel cooling mechanism and its potential applications in atomic physics and quantum technology.

text: This study presents a comprehensive approach towards realizing universal topological quantum computation using a superconductor/Abelian quantum Hall heterostructure. The research focuses on leveraging the unique properties of Abelian quantum Hall states to construct a scalable quantum computing platform. We describe the fabrication and characterization of the heterostructure, which incorporates elements such as high-temperature superconductors and two-dimensional electron gases. Our methodology involves precise control over the heterostructure's electronic structure through gate voltages and magnetic fields, enabling the manipulation of topological excitations known as Majorana zero modes. These Majorana modes serve as qubits, facilitating fault-tolerant quantum operations. The results demonstrate the successful implementation of basic quantum logic gates, including controlled-NOT (CNOT) gates, which are essential for universal quantum computation. Key insights include the robustness of these qubits against local perturbations and their compatibility with current semiconductor processing techniques, paving the way for the integration of topological qubits into existing semiconductor-based electronics. This work thus establishes a foundational model for the realization of a scalable topological quantum computer utilizing a superconductor/Abelian quantum Hall heterostructure.

[Abridged] Context. The young systems PZ Tel and HD 1160, hosting known
low-mass companions, were observed during the commissioning of the new planet
finder SPHERE with several imaging and spectroscopic modes. Aims. We aim to

use SPHERE commissioning data and REM observations, as well as literature and

Tel B allows us to revise its properties: spectral type M7+/-1, Teff=2700+/-100
K, log(g)<4.5 dex, log(L/L_Sun)=-2.51+/-0.10 dex, and mass 38-72 MJ. The 1-3.8
mic SED of HD 1160 B suggests a massive brown dwarf or a low-mass star with
spectral type M5.5-7.0, Teff=3000+/-100 K, [M/H]=-0.5-0.0 dex,

Kitaev, Liese, Remmel, and Sagan recently defined generalized factor order on
words comprised of letters from a partially ordered set $(P, \leq_P)$ by
setting $u \leq_P w$ if there is a subword $v$ of $w$ of the same length as $u$
such that the $i$-th character of $v$ is greater than or equal to the $i$-th
character of $u$ for all $i$. This subword $v$ is called an embedding of $u$
into $w$. For the case where $P$ is the positive integers with the usual
ordering, they defined the weight of a word $w = w_1\ldots w_n$ to be
$\text{wt}(w) = x^{\sum_{i=1}^n w_i} t^{n}$, and the corresponding weight
generating function $F(u;t,x) = \sum_{w \geq_P u} \text{wt}(w)$. They then
defined two words $u$ and $v$ to be Wilf equivalent, denoted $u \backsim v$, if
and only if $F(u;t,x) = F(v;t,x)$. They also defined the related generating
function $S(u;t,x) = \sum_{w \in \mathcal{S}(u)} \text{wt}(w)$ where
$\mathcal{S}(u)$ is the set of all words $w$ such that the only embedding of
$u$ into $w$ is a suffix of $w$, and showed that $u \backsim v$ if and only if
$S(u;t,x) = S(v;t,x)$. We continue this study by giving an explicit formula for
$S(u;t,x)$ if $u$ factors into a weakly increasing word followed by a weakly
decreasing word. We use this formula as an aid to classify Wilf equivalence for
all words of length 3. We also show that coefficients of related generating
functions are well-known sequences in several special cases. Finally, we
discuss a conjecture that if $u \backsim v$ then $u$ and $v$ must be
rearrangements, and the stronger conjecture that there also must be a
weight-preserving bijection $f: \mathcal{S}(u) \rightarrow \mathcal{S}(v)$ such
that $f(u)$ is a rearrangement of $u$ for all $u$.

We measure the absolute magnitude, $H$, distribution, $dN(H) \propto
10^{\alpha H}$ of the scattering Trans-Neptunian Objects (TNOs) as a proxy for
their size-frequency distribution. We show that the H-distribution of the
scattering TNOs is not consistent with a single-slope distribution, but must
transition around $H_g \sim 9$ to either a knee with a shallow slope or to a
divot, which is a differential drop followed by second exponential
distribution. Our analysis is based on a sample of 22 scattering TNOs drawn
from three different TNO surveys, the Canada-France Ecliptic Plane Survey
(CFEPS, Petit et al. 2011), Alexandersen et al. (2014), and the Outer Solar
System Origins Survey (OSSOS, Bannister et al. 2016), all of which provide well
characterized detection thresholds, combined with a cosmogonic model for the
formation of the scattering TNO population. Our measured absolute magnitude
distribution result is independent of the choice of cosmogonic model. Based on
our analysis, we estimate that number of scattering TNOs is (2.4-8.3)$\times
10^5$ for $H_r < 12$. A divot $H$-distribution is seen in a variety of
formation scenarios and may explain several puzzles in Kuiper Belt science. We
find that a divot $H$-distribution simultaneously explains the observed
scattering TNO, Neptune Trojan, Plutino, and Centaur $H$-distributions while
simultaneously predicting a large enough scattering TNO population to act as
the sole supply of the Jupiter-Family Comets.

One key challenge in talent search is how to translate complex criteria of a
hiring position into a search query. This typically requires deep knowledge on
which skills are typically needed for the position, what are their
alternatives, which companies are likely to have such candidates, etc. However,
listing examples of suitable candidates for a given position is a relatively
easy job. Therefore, in order to help searchers overcome this challenge, we
design a next generation of talent search paradigm at LinkedIn: Search by Ideal
Candidates. This new system only needs the searcher to input one or several
examples of suitable candidates for the position. The system will generate a
query based on the input candidates and then retrieve and rank results based on
the query as well as the input candidates. The query is also shown to the
searcher to make the system transparent and to allow the searcher to interact
with it. As the searcher modifies the initial query and makes it deviate from
the ideal candidates, the search ranking function dynamically adjusts an
refreshes the ranking results balancing between the roles of query and ideal
candidates. As of writing this paper, the new system is being launched to our
customers.

text: Our work investigates the phenomenon of giant dielectric anisotropy achieved through homogenization. We aim to address the challenge of enhancing the dielectric anisotropy in materials, which is crucial for various applications in electronics and photonics. By employing a homogenization approach, we demonstrate a significant increase in the dielectric anisotropy of the material, surpassing traditional limits. Through numerical simulations and analytical modeling, we systematically analyze the factors influencing the dielectric anisotropy enhancement, such as the geometric arrangement of the microstructures and the homogenization process parameters.  Our results reveal a novel method to tailor the dielectric properties of materials by manipulating their microstructure, enabling the realization of giant dielectric anisotropy. This advancement opens up new possibilities for designing high-performance devices that rely on anisotropic dielectric properties, including antennas, sensors, and optical devices. The proposed methodology not only offers a theoretical understanding of the mechanisms behind the giant dielectric anisotropy but also provides practical guidelines for the fabrication of materials with superior dielectric properties. In conclusion, our research sheds light on the potential of homogenization techniques in engineering materials with unprecedented dielectric anisotropy, paving the way for innovative applications in modern technology.

text: This research paper presents the NuGrid Stellar Data Set focusing on stellar yields ranging from hydrogen to bismuth for stellar models with initial masses from 1 to 25 solar masses and metallicities spanning from 0.0001 to 0.02. The objective of this study is to comprehensively analyze the stellar yields of elements across a wide range of masses and metallicities to enhance our understanding of nucleosynthesis in stars.   The methodology involves utilizing NuGrid's extensive nucleosynthesis calculations incorporating updated reaction rates and nuclear physics inputs to determine the stellar yields of elements. These yields are crucial for advancing our knowledge of elemental production in stars and enriching the field of astrophysics.  Key findings reveal the detailed stellar yields of elements such as helium, carbon, oxygen, iron, and heavier elements up to bismuth for various stellar models with diverse initial masses and metallicities. The results offer insights into the nucleosynthetic processes occurring in stars and provide valuable data for interpreting astronomical observations and enriching theoretical stellar evolution models.  In conclusion, this study contributes essential stellar yield data for a wide range of elements, shedding light on nucleosynthesis in stars with different masses and metallicities. The NuGrid Stellar Data Set enables a deeper understanding of elemental production in stellar evolution and enriches the field of astrophysics with valuable insights into the chemical enrichment history of galaxies.

text: In this study, we propose a novel probabilistic temporal logic augmented with frequency operators, aimed at enhancing the expressiveness and applicability of formal verification in stochastic systems. The expressiveness of traditional temporal logics is expanded by incorporating frequency operators that allow precise specification of behavioral patterns occurring at certain frequencies. We develop a comprehensive model-checking framework that efficiently evaluates these logic specifications against given stochastic models. Our approach uniquely enables the analysis of systems where evaluating the frequency of events is crucial, such as in performance analysis and reliability assessment in probabilistic systems. We employ a combination of symbolic and statistical model-checking techniques to manage the computational complexity inherent in verifying large-scale systems. We introduce an innovative algorithm integrating the frequency operators with existing probabilistic verification techniques, thereby facilitating a more robust and detailed analysis. The experimental results, obtained by applying our framework to benchmark models, demonstrate improved efficiency and scalability in comparison to existing methodologies. We further validate our approach by providing extensive empirical evidence of its applicability in real-world scenarios. Statistical evidence from our experiments indicates that our method not only maintains accuracy in verification tasks but also significantly reduces computation time, thus making it feasible for practical applications in larger and more complex systems. By advancing the capabilities of probabilistic temporal logic, our work opens new avenues for the precise specification and verification of dynamic behaviors with frequency constraints in stochastic systems, contributing significantly to the field of formal verification.

text: This study investigates the initial conditions of inflation that could lead to suppressed large-scale cosmic microwave background (CMB) fluctuations. We explore various models of inflationary potentials and their corresponding reheating processes to determine how these parameters influence the CMB power spectrum. Our analysis indicates that steep inflationary potentials, characterized by high values of the potential energy at early times, can result in suppressed CMB fluctuations. Additionally, we find that efficient reheating mechanisms, such as those involving leptogenesis or decay of light fields, play a crucial role in ensuring the observed level of primordial perturbations. The key methodology involves detailed numerical simulations of inflationary models, coupled with state-of-the-art cosmological codes to compute the resulting CMB spectra. These findings suggest that specific inflationary scenarios can be ruled out based on current CMB data, thereby narrowing down the landscape of viable inflationary models.

text: Energy dissipation and Landau damping are crucial phenomena in understanding plasma turbulence in both two- and three-dimensional systems. This research paper aims to investigate the behavior of energy dissipation and Landau damping in such turbulent plasma environments. The methodology involves numerical simulations using advanced computational models to analyze the energy transfer mechanisms and damping processes in different dimensional plasma turbulence scenarios. The key findings reveal that energy dissipation mechanisms are notably different between two- and three-dimensional plasma turbulence, with Landau damping playing a significant role in the energy exchange processes. The study also demonstrates that the presence of Landau damping leads to more efficient energy dissipation in three-dimensional plasma turbulence compared to the two-dimensional case. Moreover, the results highlight the complex interplay between energy dissipation mechanisms and Landau damping effects in turbulent plasma systems. In conclusion, a comprehensive understanding of energy dissipation and Landau damping in two- and three-dimensional plasma turbulence is essential for advancing knowledge in plasma physics and related fields.

text: We present an in-depth analysis of the global structure of Kerr-de Sitter (KdS) spacetimes, exploring their geometric and topological properties. Specifically, we focus on the interplay of ergosurfaces, event horizons, and conformal infinities, shedding light on the presence and structure of these features for various KdS solutions.  Our investigation employs several methods, including the examination of the equations of the Kasner-like regions near the horizons and the study of the properties of KdS solutions in the limit of vanishing cosmological constant. We find that the ergosurfaces and event horizons exhibit intricate patterns and display a rich interplay, exhibiting several distinct regimes depending on the values of the mass and cosmological constant.  Furthermore, we demonstrate the existence of an additional horizon, the KdS Cauchy horizon, which arises as a result of the nontrivial interplay between the cosmological and rotating components of KdS spacetimes. We investigate its properties and implications, revealing its role as a boundary for causally disconnected regions of the spacetime.  Our work contributes significantly to the understanding of the global structure of KdS spacetimes and highlights their unique properties compared to their Minkowski and Schwarzschild counterparts. By providing a comprehensive analysis of these features, we lay the foundation for further investigations into the thermodynamics, quantum properties, and other aspects of these fascinating solutions to Einstein's field equations.  Our study reveals that the KdS spacetime exhibits a rich global structure with intricately intertwined ergosurfaces, event horizons, and the newly identified KdS Cauchy horizon, contributing to a deeper understanding of the underlying physics and paving the way for future research in the field of general relativity and black hole mechanics.

Spherically symmetric equilibrium configurations of perfect fluid obeying a
polytropic equation of state are studied in spacetimes with a repulsive
cosmological constant. The configurations are specified in terms of three
parameters---the polytropic index $n$, the ratio of central pressure and
central energy density of matter $\sigma$, and the ratio of energy density of
vacuum and central density of matter $\lambda$. The static equilibrium
configurations are determined by two coupled first-order nonlinear differential
equations that are solved by numerical methods with the exception of polytropes
with $n=0$ corresponding to the configurations with a uniform distribution of
energy density, when the solution is given in terms of elementary functions.
The geometry of the polytropes is conveniently represented by embedding
diagrams of both the ordinary space geometry and the optical reference geometry
reflecting some dynamical properties of the geodesic motion. The polytropes are
represented by radial profiles of energy density, pressure, mass, and metric
coefficients. For all tested values of $n>0$, the static equilibrium
configurations with fixed parameters $n$, $\sigma$, are allowed only up to a
critical value of the cosmological parameter
$\lambda_{\mathrm{c}}=\lambda_{\mathrm{c}}(n,\sigma)$. In the case of $n>3$,
the critical value $\lambda_{\mathrm{c}}$ tends to zero for special values of
$\sigma$. The gravitational potential energy and the binding energy of the
polytropes are determined and studied by numerical methods. We discuss in
detail the polytropes with an extension comparable to those of the dark matter
halos related to galaxies, i.e., with extension $\ell > 100\,\mathrm{kpc}$ and
mass $M > 10^{12}\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$. ...

The phonon dynamics of the low-temperature superconductor Sr$_{2}$RuO$_{4}$
is calculated quantitatively in linear response theory and compared with the
structurally isomorphic high-temperature superconductor La$_{2}$CuO$_{4}$. Our
calculation corrects for a typical deficit of LDA-based calculations which
always predict a too large electronic $k_{z}$-dispersion insufficient to
describe the c-axis response in the real materials. With a more realistic
computation of the electronic band structure the frequency and wavevector
dependent irreducible polarization part of the density response function is
determined and used for adiabatic and nonadiabatic phonon calculations. Our
analysis for Sr$_{2}$RuO$_{4}$ reveals important differences from the lattice
dynamics of $p$- and $n$-doped cuprates. Consistent with experimental evidence
from inelastic neutron scattering the anomalous doping related softening of the
strongly coupling high-frequency oxygen bond-stretching modes (OBSM) which is
generic for the cuprate superconductors is largely suppressed or completely
absent, respectively, depending on the actual value of the on-site Coulomb
repulsion of the Ru4d orbitals. Also the presence of a characteristic
$\Lambda_{1}$-mode with a very steep dispersion coupling strongly with the
electrons is missing in Sr$_{2}$RuO$_{4}$. Moreover, we evaluate the
possibility of a phonon-plasmon scenario for Sr$_{2}$RuO$_{4}$ which has been
shown recently to be realistic for La$_{2}$CuO$_{4}$. In contrast to
La$_{2}$CuO$_{4}$ in Sr$_{2}$RuO$_{4}$ the very low lying plasmons are
overdamped along the c-axis.

text: We investigated the semiclassical and quantum behavior of the Mixmaster model in the polymer approach, with a focus on its dynamical properties and phase transitions. Our work aimed to elucidate the underlying mechanisms governing the model's behavior, particularly in the regime of strong nonlinearity and high polymerization degree. We employed a combination of numerical simulations and analytical techniques to study the model's dynamics, employing a modified version of the polymer approach that incorporates the Mixmaster model's stochastic dynamics.  Our results reveal that the Mixmaster model exhibits a rich and complex behavior, characterized by the emergence of chaotic attractors and phase transitions. We found that the semiclassical approximation provides a good description of the model's dynamics in the low-temperature regime, while the quantum approach yields a more accurate description in the high-temperature regime. Our numerical simulations demonstrate the importance of nonlinearity and polymerization degree in shaping the model's behavior, and we identified a critical interplay between these factors that gives rise to the observed phase transitions.  Through our analysis, we identified key features of the Mixmaster model's behavior, including the role of the stochastic dynamics in generating chaotic attractors and the impact of polymerization degree on the model's phase transitions. Our findings have implications for our understanding of the Mixmaster model's behavior in various regimes, and we propose a new framework for studying the interplay between nonlinearity, polymerization degree, and stochastic dynamics in complex systems.

Recently MV18 identified and initiated work on the new problem of
understanding structural relationships between the lattices of solutions of two
"nearby" instances of stable matching. They also gave an application of their
work to finding a robust stable matching. However, the types of changes they
allowed in going from instance $A$ to $B$ were very restricted, namely any one
agent executes an upward shift. In this paper, we allow any one agent to
permute its preference list arbitrarily. Let $M_A$ and $M_B$ be the sets of
stable matchings of the resulting pair of instances $A$ and $B$, and let
$\mathcal{L}_A$ and $\mathcal{L}_B$ be the corresponding lattices of stable
matchings. We prove that the matchings in $M_A \cap M_B$ form a sublattice of
both $\mathcal{L}_A$ and $\mathcal{L}_B$ and those in $M_A \setminus M_B$ form
a join semi-sublattice of $\mathcal{L}_A$. These properties enable us to obtain
a polynomial time algorithm for not only finding a stable matching in $M_A \cap
M_B$, but also for obtaining the partial order, as promised by Birkhoff's
Representation Theorem, thereby enabling us to generate all matchings in this
sublattice. Our algorithm also helps solve a version of the robust stable
matching problem. We discuss another potential application, namely obtaining
new insights into the incentive compatibility properties of the Gale-Shapley
Deferred Acceptance Algorithm.

text: The Off-Switch Game presents a conceptual framework at the intersection of artificial intelligence (AI), human-computer interaction, and ethical decision-making. As AI systems become increasingly autonomous, the ability for humans to intervene and effectively 'switch off' these systems becomes a critical concern. The objective of this research is to explore the dynamics and implications of maintaining human control over AI systems through the metaphorical 'off-switch'—a mechanism enabling human intervention in the operations of autonomous entities. Employing a game-theoretic approach, this study models interactions between AI systems designed with a default off-switch option and the human operators managing them. Our methodology involves constructing a series of experimental simulations to analyze the strategic decisions made by both human players and AI agents within controlled scenarios, assessing factors such as trust, dependency, and predictability. Key findings suggest that incorporating an off-switch can enhance the safety and reliability of AI systems, but its effectiveness is significantly influenced by the structure of interaction protocols and the level of transparency between the system and operator. Furthermore, the presence of an off-switch can alter the perceived agency and accountability in AI-human collaboration. The research concludes that while the implementation of an off-switch is vital for ensuring human oversight, it requires comprehensive design considerations, highlighting the balance between autonomy and control crucial for the responsible development of AI technologies. These insights contribute to the broader discourse on ethical AI deployment and the design of systems that reinforce human-centered oversight.

text: We present a novel approach to detecting, recognizing, and tracking moving objects from real-time video via a visual vocabulary model and a species-inspired particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm. Our method leverages the strengths of visual vocabulary models in object representation and classification, while incorporating the adaptability and optimization capabilities of species-inspired PSO to improve tracking performance.   Our approach begins by constructing a visual vocabulary model that represents the visual features of objects in the video stream. This model enables efficient object representation and classification, allowing us to accurately identify and track moving objects. To improve tracking performance, we employ a species-inspired PSO algorithm that adapts to the changing characteristics of the objects and the video stream. This algorithm enables the PSO particles to explore the solution space more effectively, leading to improved object tracking accuracy.  Our experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed approach in detecting, recognizing, and tracking moving objects from real-time video. We achieve state-of-the-art performance in terms of accuracy, speed, and robustness, outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods. Our approach also exhibits robustness to varying lighting conditions, occlusions, and camera motion, making it suitable for real-world applications. Overall, our method provides a novel and efficient solution for object tracking from real-time video, and has significant implications for applications such as surveillance, robotics, and computer vision.

The nearby (d = 7.7 pc) A3V star Fomalhaut is orbited by a resolved dusty
debris disk and a controversial candidate extrasolar planet. The commonly cited
age for the system (200+-100 Myr) from Barrado y Navascues et al. (1997) relied
on a combination of isochronal age plus youth indicators for the K4V common
proper motion system TW PsA. TW PsA is 1.96 deg away from Fomalhaut, and was
first proposed as a companion by Luyten (1938), but the physicality of the
binarity is worth testing with modern data. I demonstrate that TW PsA is
unequivocally a physical stellar companion to Fomalhaut, with true separation
0.280+0.019-0.012 pc (57.4+3.9-2.5 kAU) and sharing velocities within 0.1+-0.5
km/s -- consistent with being a bound system. Hence, TW PsA should be
considered "Fomalhaut B". Combining modern HR diagram constraints with four
sets of evolutionary tracks, and assuming the star was born with protosolar
composition, I estimate a new isochronal age for Fomalhaut of 450+-40 Myr and
mass of 1.92+-0.02 Msun. Various stellar youth diagnostics are re-examined for
TW PsA. The star's rotation, X-ray emission, and Li abundances are consistent
with approximate ages of 410, 380, and 360 Myr, respectively, yielding a
weighted mean age of 400+-70 Myr. Combining the independent ages, I estimate a
mean age for the Fomalhaut-TW PsA binary of 440+-40 Myr. The older age implies
that substellar companions of a given mass are approximately one magnitude
fainter at IR wavelengths than previously assumed.

Sparsity-based approaches have been popular in many applications in image
processing and imaging. Compressed sensing exploits the sparsity of images in a
transform domain or dictionary to improve image recovery from undersampled
measurements. In the context of inverse problems in dynamic imaging, recent
research has demonstrated the promise of sparsity and low-rank techniques. For
example, the patches of the underlying data are modeled as sparse in an
adaptive dictionary domain, and the resulting image and dictionary estimation
from undersampled measurements is called dictionary-blind compressed sensing,
or the dynamic image sequence is modeled as a sum of low-rank and sparse (in
some transform domain) components (L+S model) that are estimated from limited
measurements. In this work, we investigate a data-adaptive extension of the L+S
model, dubbed LASSI, where the temporal image sequence is decomposed into a
low-rank component and a component whose spatiotemporal (3D) patches are sparse
in some adaptive dictionary domain. We investigate various formulations and
efficient methods for jointly estimating the underlying dynamic signal
components and the spatiotemporal dictionary from limited measurements. We also
obtain efficient sparsity penalized dictionary-blind compressed sensing methods
as special cases of our LASSI approaches. Our numerical experiments demonstrate
the promising performance of LASSI schemes for dynamic magnetic resonance image
reconstruction from limited k-t space data compared to recent methods such as
k-t SLR and L+S, and compared to the proposed dictionary-blind compressed
sensing method.

text: In this work, we present a novel approach to achieving unicast communication in ad-hoc networks within the time complexity of O(log log n) through the application of beamforming techniques. Our study addresses the significant challenge faced in wireless ad-hoc networks the efficient delivery of unicast transmissions, which is essential for improving network scalability and reducing latency. By leveraging the directional capabilities inherent in beamforming, we effectively narrow the spatial footprint of transmissions, thus minimizing interference and enhancing the signal-to-noise ratio. Our methodology involves a detailed analysis of the network's topology to dynamically adjust the beamforming parameters, which allows for precise targeting of intended receivers while mitigating the effects of both environmental and network-induced noise. We employ an iterative stratified decomposition algorithm to optimize path selection and enable asynchronous communication, which significantly contributes to reducing delivery time. The results of our simulations demonstrate that our proposed beamforming method outperforms traditional unicast transmission techniques across various network configurations, achieving a notable reduction in average transmission time and increased reliability under high node density conditions. Our findings suggest that implementing beamforming for unicast purposes in ad-hoc networks not only enhances performance but also paves the way for more efficient and scalable network communication infrastructures. This work establishes a foundational framework for future exploration of beamforming protocols in complex network environments and highlights potential adaptations for real-world applications.

text: We present the results of a comprehensive analysis of Herschel observations in the ultracompact HII region Mon R2, focusing on the detection of water in dense photon-dominated regions (PDRs). Our investigation aimed to elucidate the role of water in the formation and evolution of PDRs, which are crucial in the interstellar medium. Through a detailed examination of the Herschel Space Observatory data, we identified water emission lines in the 217 GHz and 183 GHz bands, which were previously unreported in this region.  Our analysis revealed that the water emission is concentrated in the densest parts of the PDRs, where the photon-dominated region meets the HII region. We propose that the water is formed through the photodissociation of water vapor by the intense ultraviolet radiation from the HII region, followed by the recombination of hydrogen atoms and oxygen radicals. This process is facilitated by the presence of dust grains, which act as catalysts for the chemical reactions.  Our findings suggest that the water in PDRs plays a crucial role in regulating the chemical and physical processes that occur in these regions. The detection of water in Mon R2 provides new insights into the complex chemistry of ultracompact HII regions and has significant implications for our understanding of the interstellar medium.

This article presents a semantic tracker which simultaneously tracks a single
target and recognises its category. In general, it is hard to design a tracking
model suitable for all object categories, e.g., a rigid tracker for a car is
not suitable for a deformable gymnast. Category-based trackers usually achieve
superior tracking performance for the objects of that specific category, but
have difficulties being generalised. Therefore, we propose a novel unified
robust tracking framework which explicitly encodes both generic features and
category-based features. The tracker consists of a shared convolutional network
(NetS), which feeds into two parallel networks, NetC for classification and
NetT for tracking. NetS is pre-trained on ImageNet to serve as a generic
feature extractor across the different object categories for NetC and NetT.
NetC utilises those features within fully connected layers to classify the
object category. NetT has multiple branches, corresponding to multiple
categories, to distinguish the tracked object from the background. Since each
branch in NetT is trained by the videos of a specific category or groups of
similar categories, NetT encodes category-based features for tracking. During
online tracking, NetC and NetT jointly determine the target regions with the
right category and foreground labels for target estimation. To improve the
robustness and precision, NetC and NetT inter-supervise each other and trigger
network adaptation when their outputs are ambiguous for the same image regions
(i.e., when the category label contradicts the foreground/background
classification). We have compared the performance of our tracker to other
state-of-the-art trackers on a large-scale tracking benchmark (100
sequences)---the obtained results demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed
tracker as it outperformed other 38 state-of-the-art tracking algorithms.

Given a Hilbert space operator $T$, the level sets of function
$\Psi_T(z)=\|(T-z)^{-1}\|^{-1}$ determine the so-called pseudospectra of $T$.
We set $\Psi_T$ to be zero on the spectrum of $T$. After giving some elementary
properties of $\Psi_T$ (which, as it seems, were not noticed before), we apply
them to the study of the approximation. We prove that for any operator $T$,
there is a sequence $\{T_n\}$ of finite matrices such that $\Psi_{T_n}(z)$
tends to $\Psi_{T}(z)$ uniformly on $\C$. In this proof, quasitriangular
operators play a special role. This is merely an existence result, we do not
give a concrete construction of this sequence of matrices.
  One of our main points is to show how to use infinite-dimensional operator
models in order to produce examples and counterexamples in the set of finite
matrices of large order. In particular, we get a result, which means, in a
sense, that the pseudospectrum of a nilpotent matrix can be anything one can
imagine. We also study the norms of the multipliers in the context of
Cowen--Douglas class operators. We use these results to show that, to the
opposite to the function $\Psi_{S}$, the function $\|\sqrt{S-z}\,\|$ for
certain finite matrices $S$ may oscillate arbitrarily fast even far away from
the spectrum.

The recent Belle and BaBar measurements of the branching ratio of $B^+ \to
\tau^+ \nu_\tau$ indicate a significant deviation from the Standard Model
prediction. We demonstrate that this measurement has a serious impact on models
with minimal flavor violation involving a charged Higgs boson, ruling out a
large portion of the currently-allowed parameter space. In the constrained
minimal supersymmetric standard model, this creates a tension between the
measurements of $B^+ \to \tau^+ \nu_\tau$ and the anomalous magnetic moment of
the muon, unless $\tan\beta$ is small, $\mu > 0$, and $A_0$ takes a large
negative value. In fact, a very small region of the parameter space of this
model, with small values of $m_0$ and $m_{1/2}$, survives all the constraints
at 95% C.L.. It is remarkable that this specific region is still consistent
with the lightest supersymmetric particle as the dark matter. Moreover, it
predicts observable SUSY signals in the early runs of the LHC, even perhaps at
7 TeV. We also show that a consistent explanation for the deviation of the $B^+
\to \tau^+ \nu_\tau$ branching ratio from the Standard Model can be achieved in
a non-universal Higgs mass model, which could also predict early signals of
supersymmetry at the LHC.
label: human

text: We present a comprehensive study of the enigmatic massive star system Theta 2 Orionis A, comprising a luminous blue variable (LBV) primary and a companion star of uncertain spectral type. Our research aimed to unravel the puzzle of this system's evolution, dynamics, and internal structure.   Utilizing a combination of spectroscopic and photometric observations, we analyzed the system's variability patterns and stellar activity. Our results indicate that the primary star exhibits complex and dynamic behavior, with periodic variations in luminosity and spectral lines suggestive of intense stellar wind activity.   We employed a suite of hydrodynamic simulations to model the system's internal dynamics, incorporating the effects of strong stellar winds and gravitational interactions between the two stars. These simulations reveal a complex interplay of gravitational and dynamical forces, leading to a rich and chaotic stellar environment.   Our findings suggest that the companion star is likely a compact object, possibly a neutron star or a black hole, which is dynamically interacting with the LBV primary. We propose a scenario in which the system has undergone a catastrophic merger event, resulting in the formation of a compact remnant and the subsequent ejection of a massive stellar wind.   Our research contributes to a deeper understanding of the complex dynamics and evolution of massive star systems, shedding light on the intricate processes that govern the lives of these luminous and enigmatic objects.
label: machine
