showing only a small velocity shift which is unrelated to the intrinsic
kinematics of the nebular emission. The Ly$\alpha$ extension is $\sim$4 times
larger than the continuum emission, and makes this object comparable to
low-mass LAEs at low redshift, and more compact than the Lyman-break galaxies
and Ly$\alpha$ emitters usually studied at high redshift. We model the
Ly$\alpha$ line and surface brightness profile using a radiative transfer code
in an expanding gas shell, finding that this model provides a good description

text: We investigate the relationship between the unit incomparability dimension and clique cover width in graphs, two fundamental parameters in graph theory. Through a series of experiments and case studies, we demonstrate that there is a significant correlation between the unit incomparability dimension and clique cover width. We show that graphs with higher unit incomparability dimensions tend to have wider clique cover widths, and vice versa. This relationship is particularly pronounced in graphs with a high density of edges and a large number of cliques.  Our findings have important implications for the design of efficient algorithms for graph coloring, clique detection, and other graph-theoretic problems. By understanding the interplay between unit incomparability dimension and clique cover width, we can develop more effective strategies for tackling these problems. text: We investigated the Aharonov-Bohm effect in a system of 5/2-filled charge e/4 quasiparticles in multiple small Fabry-Perot interferometers. By analyzing the interference patterns in the interferometers, we observed a clear Aharonov-Bohm effect, where the phase of the wave function is influenced by the magnetic flux through the cavity.  Our results show that the coherence length of the quasiparticles is inversely proportional to the magnetic flux, with a characteristic length scale of approximately 10 nm. This is consistent with theoretical predictions for the Aharonov-Bohm effect in a 5/2-filled system. We also observed a significant increase in the coherence length at lower temperatures, indicating that the quasiparticles are more susceptible to decoherence at higher temperatures.  Our findings have important implications for the understanding of quantum transport in topological systems and the behavior of quasiparticles in the presence of magnetic fields. The observed Aharonov-Bohm effect and coherence length provide valuable insights into the properties of charge e/4 quasiparticles in the 5/2-filled regime, and pave the way for further research into the quantum transport properties of topological systems.

text: Inflationary cosmology, a popular theory explaining the early universe's evolution, involves spontaneous symmetry breaking (SSB) during the inflaton field's false vacuum decay. This SSB process leads to the generation of fluctuations in the inflaton potential, which seeds the formation of cosmic structures. However, the fate of Goldstone Bosons (GBs), the Nambu-Goldstone (NG) modes associated with the broken symmetry, remains an open question.  In this paper, we investigate the role of GBs in the early universe during and after inflation. We consider a simplified model where the inflaton is the real part of a complex scalar field. The breaking of complex scalar field's global U(1) symmetry leads to the generation of a massless GB, the axion. We study the evolution of axion fields and their interactions with the inflaton during the false vacuum decay. We use the exact solutions of the inflationary background equations to calculate the spectrum of fluctuations generated by GBs.  Our results show that GBs can significantly affect the primordial power spectrum and the subsequent structure formation. We find that the presence of GBs leads to a modification in the spectral index and an enhancement of the power on small scales, which is consistent with current observational data. Furthermore, we discuss the possible observational consequences of our findings, including a potential link to the dark matter problem.  In conclusion, this paper provides new insights into the role of GBs in the early universe during and after inflation. We demonstrate that the presence of GBs can lead to observable effects on the primordial power spectrum and the structure formation, which opens up new avenues for exploring the implications of spontaneous symmetry breaking in cosmology.

text: We present a novel approach to handle the ingestion, indexing, and retrieval of high-velocity multidimensional sensor data on a single node. The increasing prevalence of sensors and IoT devices has led to a massive growth in high-dimensional and high-velocity data. Traditional data processing systems struggle to efficiently ingest, index, and query such data. This problem becomes even more challenging when dealing with a single node due to limited computing resources. To address these challenges, we propose a hybrid data processing pipeline. The pipeline consists of a stream processing component for real-time ingestion and a batch processing component for offline indexing and retrieval. The stream processing component processes data in real-time using sliding windows and incremental updates. It identifies anomalies and generates alerts in real-time. The batch processing component utilizes efficient indexing techniques such as R-tree and BK-tree for indexing high-dimensional data. It performs offline queries on indexed data to provide accurate and timely results. Our experimental evaluation on real-world sensor data shows that our proposed pipeline can handle high-velocity data effectively. The pipeline achieves a low latency of 150ms for real-time processing and 1.2 seconds for offline indexing and querying. Moreover, it can process data at a rate of 100,000 records per second, which is significantly higher than traditional systems. Our work provides a viable solution for handling high-velocity multidimensional sensor data on a single node and opens up new research directions for scalable and efficient data processing. Keywords high-velocity data, multidimensional sensor data, data processing, real-time processing, batch processing, stream processing, R-tree, BK-tree.

A spherical dust cloud which is initially at rest and which has a
monotonously decaying density profile collapses and forms a shell-focussing
singularity. Provided the density profile is not too flat, meaning that its
second radial derivative is negative at the center, this singularity is visible
to local, and sometimes even to global observers. According to the strong
cosmic censorship conjecture, such naked singularities should be unstable under
generic, nonspherical perturbations of the initial data or when more realistic
matter models are considered.
  In an attempt to gain some understanding about this stability issue, in this
work we initiate the analysis of a simpler but related problem. We discuss the
stability of test fields propagating in the vicinity of the Cauchy horizon
associated to the naked central singularity. We first study the high-frequency
limit and show that the fields undergo a blueshift as they approach the Cauchy
horizon. However, in contrast to what occurs at inner horizons of black holes,
we show that the blueshift is uniformly bounded along incoming and outgoing
null rays. Motivated by this boundedness result, we take a step beyond the
geometric optic approximation and consider the Cauchy evolution of spherically
symmetric test scalar fields. We prove that under reasonable conditions on the
initial data a suitable rescaled field can be continuously extended to the
Cauchy horizon. In particular, this result implies that the physical field is
everywhere finite on the Cauchy horizon away from the central singularity.

We employ N-body simulation techniques to model a variety of stellar mass loss rates, representative of different stellar classes, assessing their consequent effects on multi-planet systems. Our methodology incorporates equations of motion adjusted for continuously varying stellar mass, offering sensitivity to changes in mass loss patterns over time.  The results elucidate that planetary systems display diverse responses contingent on initial configurations and the rate of stellar mass loss. We find that eccentricities and semi-major axes of planetary orbits can undergo substantial modifications, with inner systems more prone to destabilization. Notably, resonance breaking and planet ejections emerge as frequent outcomes in systems with pronounced mass loss rates. Additionally, we observe that significant orbital expansion of remaining planets can occur, potentially enhancing habitability zones. Our findings contribute to understanding the post-main-sequence fate of planetary systems, offering insights into future observations and the potential habitability of such systems. These results underscore the importance of incorporating stellar evolution dynamics in long-term planetary system studies.

The geometry of quantum states provides a unifying framework for estimation
processes based on quantum probes, and it allows to derive the ultimate bounds
of the achievable precision. We show a relation between the statistical
distance between infinitesimally close quantum states and the second order
variation of the coherence of the optimal measurement basis with respect to the
state of the probe. In Quantum Phase Estimation protocols, this leads to
identify coherence as the relevant resource that one has to engineer and
control to optimize the estimation precision. Furthermore, the main object of
the theory i.e., the Symmetric Logarithmic Derivative, in many cases allows to
identify a proper factorization of the whole Hilbert space in two subsystems.
The factorization allows: to discuss the role of coherence vs correlations in
estimation protocols; to show how certain estimation processes can be
completely or effectively described within a single-qubit subsystem; and to
derive lower bounds for the scaling of the estimation precision with the number
of probes used. We illustrate how the framework works for both noiseless and
noisy estimation procedures, in particular those based on multi-qubit
GHZ-states. Finally we succinctly analyze estimation protocols based on
zero-temperature critical behaviour. We identify the coherence that is at the
heart of their efficiency, and we show how it exhibits the non-analyticities
and scaling behaviour proper of a large class of quantum phase transitions.

Our results indicate that the coherent control of current injection in zigzag graphene nanoribbons is feasible, paving the way for the development of novel nanoelectronic devices with tailored edge-state properties.  Our findings have significant implications for the design of topological quantum computing architectures and the exploration of edge-state manipulation in graphene-based systems. We study dynamical error suppression from the perspective of reducing
sequencing complexity, in order to facilitate efficient semi-autonomous
quantum-coherent systems. With this aim, we focus on digital sequences where
all interpulse time periods are integer multiples of a minimum clock period and
compatibility with simple digital classical control circuitry is intrinsic,
using so-called em Walsh functions as a general mathematical framework. The
Walsh functions are an orthonormal set of basis functions which may be
associated directly with the control propagator for a digital modulation
scheme, and dynamical decoupling (DD) sequences can be derived from the
locations of digital transitions therein. We characterize the suite of the
resulting Walsh dynamical decoupling (WDD) sequences, and identify the number
of periodic square-wave (Rademacher) functions required to generate a Walsh
function as the key determinant of the error-suppressing features of the
relevant WDD sequence. WDD forms a unifying theoretical framework as it
includes a large variety of well-known and novel DD sequences, providing
significant flexibility and performance benefits relative to basic
quasi-periodic design. We also show how Walsh modulation may be employed for
the protection of certain nontrivial logic gates, providing an implementation
of a dynamically corrected gate. Based on these insights we identify Walsh
modulation as a digital-efficient approach for physical-layer error
suppression.

text: Isoscalar dipole coherence plays a significant role in understanding the nuclear structure and electromagnetic properties of atomic nuclei. In this study, we investigate the isoscalar dipole coherence at low energies and forbidden E1 strength using the random-phase approximation and the quenched Skyrme Hartree-Fock method. The calculations were performed for the oxygen isotopic chain, and the results showed a gradual decrease in coherence length with the increase of neutron excess. This finding can be attributed to the neutron skin thickening and the change in nuclear shape with increasing neutron excess. Our study also reveals a negative trend of isoscalar dipole coherence length with the decrease of energy in the low-energy region. This behavior can be explained by the increasing contribution of the Pauli blocking effect and the quenching of the magnetic moment. Furthermore, we examine the forbidden E1 transitions and find that they are significantly influenced by the isoscalar dipole coherence. Our results suggest that the isoscalar dipole coherence is a crucial factor in understanding the nuclear structure and electromagnetic properties at low energies, providing insights into the underlying mechanisms of the forbidden E1 transitions and paving the way for future studies on the subject.

text: In this study, we investigate the mixing times of Markov chains on degree-constrained orientations of planar graphs. The mixing time is a fundamental concept in Markov chain theory, representing the time it takes for a Markov chain to reach a stationary distribution from an arbitrary starting point. Degree-constrained orientations are a special class of graph orientations that preserve the degree sequence of a given graph while allowing for multiple edges and self-loops. The objective of this research is to understand the relationship between the degree constraints and the mixing times of Markov chains on planar graphs. We employ two well-known Markov chains, the Glauber dynamics and the Metropolis-Hastings algorithm, to study the mixing times of degree-constrained orientations of planar graphs. Our methodology involves constructing degree-constrained orientations for several planar graphs and calculating the corresponding mixing times using simulations. Our key findings reveal that the mixing times of degree-constrained Markov chains on planar graphs are significantly larger than those of the same graphs with random orientations. Moreover, we find that graphs with higher average degrees and larger clustering coefficients have longer mixing times. Our results contribute to the growing body of research on mixing times in Markov chains and have implications for applications in areas such as statistical physics, machine learning, and network analysis. In conclusion, this study sheds light on the relationship between degree constraints and mixing times of Markov chains on planar graphs. We find that degree-constrained orientations lead to longer mixing times compared to random orientations, and that graphs with higher degrees and larger clustering coefficients have even longer mixing times. Our findings offer insights into the behavior of Markov chains on degree-constrained graphs and have implications for various applications in science and engineering.

This paper addresses the distributed frequency control problem in a
multi-area power system taking into account of unknown time-varying power
imbalance. Particularly, fast controllable loads are utilized to restore system
frequency under changing power imbalance in an optimal manner. The imbalanced
power causing frequency deviation is decomposed into three parts: a known
constant part, an unknown low-frequency variation and a high-frequency
residual. The known steady part is usually the prediction of power imbalance.
The variation may result from the fluctuation of renewable resources, electric
vehicle charging, etc., which is usually unknown to operators. The
high-frequency residual is usually unknown and treated as an external
disturbance. Correspondingly, in this paper, we resolve the following three
problems in different timescales: 1) allocate the steady part of power
imbalance economically; 2) mitigate the effect of unknown low-frequency power
variation locally; 3) attenuate unknown high-frequency disturbances. To this
end, a distributed controller combining consensus method with adaptive internal
model control is proposed. We first prove that the closed-loop system is
asymptotically stable and converges to the optimal solution of an optimization
problem if the external disturbance is not included. We then prove that the
power variation can be mitigated accurately. Furthermore, we show that the
closed-loop system is robust against both parameter uncertainty and external
disturbances. The New England system is used to verify the efficacy of our
design.

In this paper we compute two important information-theoretic quantities which
arise in the application of multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna
wireless communication systems: the distribution of the mutual information of
multi-antenna Gaussian channels, and the Gallager random coding upper bound on
the error probability achievable by finite-length channel codes. It turns out
that the mathematical problem underpinning both quantities is the computation
of certain Hankel determinants generated by deformed versions of classical
weight functions. For single-user MIMO systems, it is a deformed Laguerre
weight, whereas for multi-user MIMO systems it is a deformed Jacobi weight. We
apply two different methods to characterize each of these Hankel determinants.
First, we employ the ladder operators of the corresponding monic orthogonal
polynomials to give an exact characterization of the Hankel determinants in
terms of Painlev\'{e} differential equations. This turns out to be a
Painlev\'{e} V for the single-user MIMO scenario and a Painlev\'{e} VI for the
multi user scenario. We then employ Coulomb fluid methods to derive new
closed-form approximations for the Hankel determinants which, although formally
valid for large matrix dimensions, are shown to give accurate results for both
the MIMO mutual information distribution and the error exponent even when the
matrix dimensions are small. Focusing on the single-user mutual information
distribution, we then employ both the exact Painlev\'{e} representation and the
Coulomb fluid approximation to yield deeper insights into the scaling behavior
in terms of the number of antennas and signal-to-noise ratio. Among other
things, these results allow us to study the asymptotic Gaussianity of the
distribution as the number of antennas increase, and to explicitly compute the
correction terms to the mean, variance, and higher order cumulants.
label: human

text:
RX J0513.1+0851 and RX J0539.9+0956 were previously identified as young,
low-mass, single-lined spectroscopic binary systems and classified as
weak-lined T Tauri stars at visible wavelengths. Here we present radial
velocities, spectral types, vsini values, and flux ratios for the components in
these systems resulting from two-dimensional cross-correlation analysis. These
results are based on high-resolution, near-infrared spectroscopy taken with the
Keck II telescope to provide a first characterization of these systems as
double-lined rather than single-lined. It applies the power of infrared
spectroscopy to the detection of cool secondaries; the flux scales as a less
steep function of mass in the infrared than in the visible, thus enabling an
identification of low-mass secondaries. We found that the RX J0513.1+0851 and
RX J0539.9+0956 primary stars are fast rotators, 60 km/s and 80 km/s
respectively; this introduces extra difficulty in the detection of the
secondary component as a result of the quite broad absorption lines. To date,
these are the highest rotational velocities measured for a pre-main sequence
spectroscopic binary. The orbital parameters and mass ratios were determined by
combining new visible light spectroscopy with our infrared data for both
systems. For RX J0513.1+0851, we derived a period of ~4 days and a mass ratio
of q = 0.46 +/- 0.01 and for RX J0539.9+0956, a period of ~1117 days and a mass
ratio of q = 0.66 +/- 0.01. Based on our derived properties for the stellar
components, we estimate the luminosities and hence distances to these binaries
at 220 pc and 90 pc. They appear to be significantly closer than previously
estimated.
label: human

text: This study investigates the computational complexity of super-coherence problems within Answer Set Programming (ASP). We begin by presenting a comprehensive overview of super-coherence, a fundamental concept in ASP that ensures consistency among rules and facts. Our work attempts to classify these problems into complexity classes, aiming to understand their inherent difficulty levels. We employ various proof techniques and reductions to establish the boundaries of tractability and NP-hardness. Key methodologies include exploring the impact of different rule structures on problem complexity and analyzing how varying input sizes affect computational requirements. The results reveal distinct complexity profiles across different scenarios, providing insights into which configurations are more amenable to efficient solution methods. These findings contribute to a deeper understanding of the algorithmic challenges associated with super-coherence in ASP, paving the way for more targeted research and practical applications.
label: machine

text:
The free energy cost of confining a star polymer where $f$ flexible polymer
chains containing $N$ monomeric units are tethered to a central unit in a slit
with two parallel repulsive walls a distance $D$ apart is considered, for good
solvent conditions. Also the parallel and perpendicular components of the
gyration radius of the star polymer, and the monomer density profile across the
slit are obtained. Theoretical descriptions via Flory theory and scaling
treatments are outlined, and compared to numerical self-consistent field
calculations (applying the Scheutjens-Fleer lattice theory) and to Molecular
Dynamics results for a bead-spring model. It is shown that Flory theory and
self-consistent field (SCF) theory yield the correct scaling of the parallel
linear dimension of the star with $N$, $f$ and $D$, but cannot be used for
estimating the free energy cost reliably. We demonstrate that the same problem
occurs already for the confinement of chains in cylindrical tubes. We also
briefly discuss the problem of a free or grafted star polymer interacting with
a single wall, and show that the dependence of confining force on the
functionality of the star is different for a star confined in a nanoslit and a
star interacting with a single wall, which is due to the absence of a symmetry
plane in the latter case.

text: This study reports the design, fabrication, and testing of a 10B-based neutron detector consisting of a stack of Multi-wire Proportional Counters (MWPCs) and macrostructured cathodes. Neutron detection using 10B-activated scintillator offers the advantages of low gamma background, high neutron sensitivity, and excellent time resolution. To improve the detector's performance, we employed a macrostructured cathode design, which increased the detector's effective area and reduced the readout noise.      The MWPCs were fabricated using standard microfabrication techniques, and the macrostructured cathodes were formed by electroplating copper onto the cathode surface. The cathodes were designed to provide an increased collecting area, allowing for better charge collection and reduced electron drift times. The detector was assembled using copper bonding to connect the MWPCs and cathodes.      The detector's response to neutrons was measured using a calibrated Am-Be neutron source. The results showed a high detection efficiency, with the detector able to distinguish neutrons from gamma rays with a high degree of accuracy. The time resolution was found to be 2.2 ns, which is faster than most other neutron detectors. The readout noise was also significantly reduced due to the use of the macrostructured cathodes.      The findings of this study demonstrate the feasibility of using stacked MWPCs and macrostructured cathodes in 10B-based neutron detectors. This design can provide high neutron sensitivity, excellent time resolution, and low gamma background, making it an attractive option for applications in neutron imaging and spectroscopy. Further work is ongoing to explore the potential for scaling up the design to larger detector sizes and improving the fabrication process to achieve better uniformity and higher resolution.

We present a new millimeter CO-line observation towards supernova remnant
(SNR) CTB 87, which was regarded purely as a pulsar wind nebula (PWN), and an
optical investigation of a coincident surrounding superbubble. The CO
observation shows that the SNR delineated by the radio emission is projectively
covered by a molecular cloud (MC) complex at V$_{\rm {LSR}}$ = $-60$ to $-54$
km s$^{-1}$. Both the symmetric axis of the radio emission and the trailing
X-ray PWN appear projectively to be along a gap between two molecular gas
patches at $-58$ to $-57$ km s$^{-1}$. Asymmetric broad profiles of $^{12}$CO
lines peaked at $-58$ km s$^{-1}$ are found at the eastern and southwestern
edges of the radio emission. This represents a kinematic signature consistent
with an SNR-MC interaction. We also find that a superbubble, $\sim 37'$ in
radius, appears to surround the SNR from HI 21cm (V$_{\rm {LSR}} \sim -61$ to
$-68$ km s$^{-1}$), WISE mid-IR, and optical extinction data. We build a
multi-band photometric stellar sample of stars within the superbubble region
and find 82 OB star candidates. The likely peak distance in the stars'
distribution seems consistent with the distance previously suggested for CTB
87. We suggest the arc-like radio emission is mainly the relic of the part of
blastwave that propagates into the MC complex and is now in a radiative stage
while the other part of blastwave has been expanding into the low-density
region in the superbubble. This scenario naturally explains the lack of the
X-ray emission related to the ejecta and blastwave. The SNR-MC interaction also
favours a hadronic contribution to the {\gamma}-ray emission from the CTB 87
region.
label: human

text:
Quantum field theory predicts Weyl semimetals to possess a peculiar response
of the longitudinal current density to the application of a DC magnetic field.
Such a response function has been shown to be at odds with a general result
showing the vanishing of the bulk current in an equilibrium system on any real
material with a lattice in an external magnetic field. Here we resolve this
apparent contradiction by introducing a model where a current flows in response
to a magnetic field even without Weyl nodes. We point out that the previous
derivation of a vanishing CME in the limit of vanishing real frequency is a
consequence of the assumption of periodic boundary conditions of the system. A
more realistic system with open boundary conditions is not subject to these
constraints and can have a non-vanishing CME. Consistent with recent work, we
found the finite frequency CME to be non-vanishing in general when there was a
non-vanishing Berry curvature on the Fermi surface. This does not necessitate
having a topological Berry flux as in the case of a Weyl node. Finally, we
study how the perturbation theory in magnetic field might be more stable in the
presence of disorder. Using the standard diagrammatic treatment of disorder
within the Born approximation, we have found that in a realistic disordered
system, the chiral magnetic response is really a dynamical phenomena and
vanishes in the DC limit.
label: human

text: We present a novel approach to detecting zones and threats on 3D body scans for enhanced security in airports utilizing deep machine learning techniques. Our method leverages a multi-modal fusion framework, integrating 3D body scans, facial recognition, and behavioral analysis to identify potential security risks. We employ a deep neural network architecture, combining convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and recurrent neural networks (RNNs) to learn complex patterns and relationships within the multi-modal data.  Through extensive experimentation, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in detecting zones and threats on 3D body scans, achieving an average accuracy of 95.6% and 92.1% for threat detection and zone identification, respectively. Our results outperform state-of-the-art methods in the literature, showcasing the superiority of our multi-modal fusion framework in capturing nuanced security threats. Notably, we observe significant improvements in detection accuracy when incorporating facial recognition and behavioral analysis, highlighting the value of multi-modal approaches in enhancing security.  Our approach is trained on a large-scale dataset of 3D body scans, facial images, and behavioral data, ensuring robustness and generalizability. We also explore the impact of various hyperparameters and model architectures on performance, providing insights into the optimal configuration for real-world deployments. Our findings have significant implications for airport security, enabling the development of more effective and efficient threat detection systems that can adapt to evolving security threats.
label: machine

The computation of the geometric transformation between a reference and a
target image, known as registration or alignment, corresponds to the projection
of the target image onto the transformation manifold of the reference image
(the set of images generated by its geometric transformations). It, however,
often takes a nontrivial form such that the exact computation of projections on
the manifold is difficult. The tangent distance method is an effective
algorithm to solve this problem by exploiting a linear approximation of the
manifold. As theoretical studies about the tangent distance algorithm have been
largely overlooked, we present in this work a detailed performance analysis of
this useful algorithm, which can eventually help its implementation. We
consider a popular image registration setting using a multiscale pyramid of
lowpass filtered versions of the (possibly noisy) reference and target images,
which is particularly useful for recovering large transformations. We first
show that the alignment error has a nonmonotonic variation with the filter
size, due to the opposing effects of filtering on both manifold nonlinearity
and image noise. We then study the convergence of the multiscale tangent
distance method to the optimal solution. We finally examine the performance of
the tangent distance method in image classification applications. Our
theoretical findings are confirmed by experiments on image transformation
models involving translations, rotations and scalings. Our study is the first
detailed study of the tangent distance algorithm that leads to a better
understanding of its efficacy and to the proper selection of its design
parameters.
label: human

text: In this work, we present a novel approach to constraining cosmological parameters using the clustering statistics of luminous red galaxies (LRGs) from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS). We aim to address existing limitations in large-scale structure analyses by developing a comprehensive framework that incorporates an improved treatment of systematic effects and non-linearities in clustering data. Employing a modified likelihood function, we rigorously analyze the two-point correlation function and power spectrum of the LRG sample, which provides enhanced sensitivity to baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) and redshift-space distortions (RSD). Our results yield tight constraints on the matter density parameter (Ω_m), the baryon fraction (Ω_b), and the scalar spectral index (n_s), with unprecedented precision. Crucially, we demonstrate significant improvements in the determination of the Hubble constant (H_0) and the dark energy equation of state parameter (w) through our method. By incorporating additional systematic corrections and utilizing a robust Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) technique, we reduce potential biases inherent in prior analyses. Our findings are consistent with contemporary cosmological models, providing critical insights into the composition and evolution of the universe. This refined methodology establishes a benchmark for future analyses of galaxy clustering, highlighting the power of LRGs as cosmological probes. The enhanced understanding of large-scale structure achieved through our approach paves the way for more accurate predictions of cosmic evolution and insights into dark energy dynamics, underscoring the need for meticulous treatment of clustering data in ongoing and future galaxy surveys.
label: machine

text: We investigate the implications of one loop tests of higher spin theories within the AdS/CFT framework, seeking to deepen our understanding of holographic dualities. Our work addresses the long-standing challenge of elucidating the behavior of higher spin gauge theories and their corresponding conformal field theories (CFTs) at one-loop order. By applying functional methods, we derive the one-loop corrections to the partition function of higher spin gauge fields in Anti-de Sitter (AdS) space and systematically analyze their contributions to the boundary correlation functions. Our results demonstrate that higher spin interactions significantly modify the structure of correlators in the CFT, revealing unexpected non-local features. We explore the consistency of our findings with the flat space limit, affirming the robustness of the holographic principles at play. We also calculus the anomalies generated at one loop and their implications on the conformal symmetry, presenting evidence that supports the interplay between higher spin gravity and quantum anomalies in the boundary theory. Our methodology encompasses both analytic and numerical approaches, providing detailed calculations of the relevant Feynman diagrams and exploring potential implications for the consistency of higher spin theories. Ultimately, our results pave the way for further exploration of the role of higher spin fields in the context of quantum gravity and strengthen the connection between higher spin theories and fundamental questions in string theory and quantum field theory.
label: machine

We consider fragments of first-order logic and as models we allow finite and
infinite words simultaneously. The only binary relations apart from equality
are order comparison < and the successor predicate +1. We give
characterizations of the fragments Sigma2 = Sigma2[<,+1] and FO2 = FO2[<,+1] in
terms of algebraic and topological properties. To this end we introduce the
factor topology over infinite words. It turns out that a language L is in the
intersection of FO2 and Sigma2 if and only if L is the interior of an FO2
language. Symmetrically, a language is in the intersection of FO2 and Pi2 if
and only if it is the topological closure of an FO2 language. The fragment
Delta2, which by definition is the intersection of Sigma2 and Pi2 contains
exactly the clopen languages in FO2. In particular, over infinite words Delta2
is a strict subclass of FO2. Our characterizations yield decidability of the
membership problem for all these fragments over finite and infinite words; and
as a corollary we also obtain decidability for infinite words. Moreover, we
give a new decidable algebraic characterization of dot-depth 3/2 over finite
words. Decidability of dot-depth 3/2 over finite words was first shown by
Gla{\ss}er and Schmitz in STACS 2000, and decidability of the membership
problem for FO2 over infinite words was shown 1998 by Wilke in his habilitation
thesis whereas decidability of Sigma2 over infinite words was not known before.
label: human

text:
The photometric and spectroscopic evolution of the He/N and very fast Nova
Cyg 2008 N2 (V2491 Cyg) is studied in detail. A primary maximum was reached at
V=7.45 +/-0.05 on April 11.37 (+/-0.1) 2008 UT, followed by a smooth decline
characterized by t2(V)=4.8 days, and then a second maximum was attained at
V=9.49 +/-0.03, 14.5 days after the primary one. This is the only third nova to
have displayed a secondary maximum, after V2362 Cyg and V1493 Aql. The
development and energetics of the secondary maximum is studied in detail. The
smooth decline that followed was accurately monitored until day +144 when the
nova was 8.6 mag fainter than maximum brightness, well into its nebular phase,
with its line and continuum emissivity declining as t-3. The reddening
affecting the nova was E(B-V)=0.23 +/-0.01, and the distance of 14 kpc places
the nova at a height above the galactic plane of 1.1 kpc, larger than typical
for He/N novae. The expansion velocity of the bulk of ejecta was 2000 km/sec,
with complex emission profiles and weak P-Cyg absorptions during the optically
thick phase, and saddle-like profiles during the nebular phase.
Photo-ionization analysis of the emission line spectrum indicates that the mass
ejected by the outburst was 5.3 10(-6) Msun and the mass fractions to be
X=0.573, Y=0.287, Z=0.140, with those of individual elements being N=0.074,
O=0.049, Ne=0.015. The metallicity of the accreted material was [Fe/H]=-0.25,
in line with ambient value at the nova galacto-centric distance. Additional
spectroscopic and photometric observations at days +477 and +831 show the nova
returned to the brightness level of the progenitor and to have resumed the
accretion onto the white dwarf.

text: The abstract focuses on the study of the interstellar environment surrounding the supernova remnant CTB 87. The investigation aims to understand the physical conditions and dynamics within the remnant’s surroundings, including the distribution and properties of gas, dust, and magnetic fields. Utilizing multi-wavelength observations and numerical simulations, the research explores the role of the interstellar medium in shaping the remnant's structure and evolution. Key findings include the identification of distinct regions with enhanced density and temperature gradients, as well as the detection of ionized gas structures indicative of ongoing shock-heating processes. The study also reveals the presence of complex magnetic field configurations that could influence particle acceleration mechanisms. Ultimately, the research contributes to our understanding of supernova remnant formation and evolution within their cosmic context.

We perform particle-in-cell simulations of perpendicular nonrelativistic
collisionless shocks to study electron heating and pre-acceleration for
parameters that permit extrapolation to the conditions at young supernova
remnants. Our high-resolution large-scale numerical experiments sample a
representative portion of the shock surface and demonstrate that the efficiency
of electron injection is strongly modulated with the phase of the shock
reformation. For plasmas with low and moderate temperature (plasma beta
$\beta_{\rm p}=5\cdot 10^{-4}$ and $\beta_{\rm p}=0.5$), we explore the
nonlinear shock structure and electron pre-acceleration for various
orientations of the large-scale magnetic field with respect to the simulation
plane while keeping it at $90^\circ$ to the shock normal. Ion reflection off
the shock leads to the formation of magnetic filaments in the shock ramp,
resulting from Weibel-type instabilities, and electrostatic Buneman modes in
the shock foot. In all cases under study, the latter provides first-stage
electron energization through the shock-surfing acceleration (SSA) mechanism.
The subsequent energization strongly depends on the field orientation and
proceeds through adiabatic or second-order Fermi acceleration processes for
configurations with the out-of-plane and in-plane field components,
respectively. For strictly out-of-plane field the fraction of supra-thermal
electrons is much higher than for other configurations, because only in this
case the Buneman modes are fully captured by the 2D simulation grid. Shocks in
plasma with moderate $\beta_{\rm p}$ provide more efficient pre-acceleration.
The relevance of our results to the physics of fully three-dimensional systems
is discussed.
label: human

text:
Different approaches have improved the sensitivity of either electron or
nuclear magnetic resonance to the single spin level. For optical detection it
has essentially become routine to observe a single electron spin or nuclear
spin. Typically, the systems in use are carefully designed to allow for single
spin detection and manipulation, and of those systems, diamond spin defects
rank very high, being so robust that they can be addressed, read out and
coherently controlled even under ambient conditions and in a versatile set of
nanostructures. This renders them as a new type of sensor, which has been shown
to detect single electron and nuclear spins among other quantities like force,
pressure and temperature. Adapting pulse sequences from classic NMR and EPR,
and combined with high resolution optical microscopy, proximity to the target
sample and nanoscale size, the diamond sensors have the potential to constitute
a new class of magnetic resonance detectors with single spin sensitivity. As
diamond sensors can be operated under ambient conditions, they offer potential
application across a multitude of disciplines. Here we review the different
existing techniques for magnetic resonance, with a focus on diamond defect spin
sensors, showing their potential as versatile sensors for ultra-sensitive
magnetic resonance with nanoscale spatial resolution.
label: human

text:
Quasi-realistic string models in the free fermionic formulation typically
contain an anomalous U(1), which gives rise to a Fayet-Iliopoulos D-term that
breaks supersymmetry at the one--loop level in string perturbation theory.
Supersymmetry is traditionally restored by imposing F- and D-flatness on the
vacuum. By employing the standard analysis of flat directions we present a
quasi--realistic three generation string model in which stringent F- and D-flat
solution do not appear to exist to all orders in the superpotential. We
speculate that this result is indicative of the non-existence of supersymmetric
flat F- and D-solutions in this model. We provide some arguments in support of
this scenario and discuss its potential implications. Bose-Fermi degeneracy of
the string spectrum implies that the one--loop partition function and hence the
one-loop cosmological constant vanishes in the model. If our assertion is
correct, this model may represent the first known example with vanishing
cosmological constant and perturbatively broken supersymmetry. We discuss the
distinctive properties of the internal free fermion boundary conditions that
may correspond to a large set of models that share these properties. The
geometrical moduli in this class of models are fixed due to asymmetric boundary
conditions, whereas absence of supersymmetric flat directions would imply that
the supersymmetric moduli are fixed as well and the dilaton may be fixed by
hidden sector nonperturbative effects.
label: human

text: This study presents a comprehensive census of near-infrared (NIR) RR Lyrae stars along the southern Galactic plane, aiming to shed light on the Milky Way's stellar fossil. The background of RR Lyrae stars, a type of pulsating variable, is deeply rooted in their use as distance indicators in extragalactic astronomy. However, their study has been largely confined to the northern hemisphere, leaving a significant knowledge gap in the southern region.  The objective of this research is to investigate the NIR properties and population characteristics of RR Lyrae stars along the southern Galactic plane, thereby providing insights into the Milky Way's stellar evolution and structure. To achieve this, a systematic survey of NIR RR Lyrae stars was conducted using the VISTA (Visible and Infrared Survey Telescope for Astronomy) survey data, covering an extensive area of approximately 1,500 square degrees.  Key findings of this study reveal a previously unknown population of NIR RR Lyrae stars, characterized by distinct stellar and chemical properties. The census provides new constraints on the Milky Way's stellar evolution models, highlighting the importance of southern surveys in understanding the Galaxy's structure and evolution. The results also underscore the significance of NIR observations in the study of RR Lyrae stars, offering a new window into the physics of these celestial objects. Ultimately, this study contributes to our understanding of the Milky Way's stellar fossil, highlighting the importance of continued southern surveys in astronomy.
label: machine

text: This research paper explores the application of provenance-based security monitoring techniques in retrofitting existing applications to enhance their security posture. The study aims to address the challenge of securing legacy systems that lack built-in security features, focusing on the integration of provenance tracking into application development and runtime environments. The methodology involves the implementation of provenance-based security tools within a set of real-world applications, followed by comprehensive testing and analysis to evaluate the effectiveness of these enhancements. Key findings indicate significant improvements in identifying unauthorized access attempts and anomalous behavior, which were previously undetected due to the lack of robust security mechanisms. The research concludes with recommendations for integrating provenance-based security monitoring as a critical component in the retrofitting process of applications to ensure enhanced security and resilience against cyber threats.
label: machine

text: Preconditioning techniques, such as SPAI (Sparse Approximation of Inverse) and PSAI (Preconditioned Sparse Approximation of Inverse), have been widely used to improve the convergence of iterative linear solvers for large sparse linear systems. However, these methods are often limited by their computational complexity and scalability for irregular sparse matrices. Irregular sparse matrices, which have a non-uniform distribution of non-zero elements, pose significant challenges to preconditioning techniques.   This research aims to develop an approach to making SPAI and PSAI preconditioning effective for large irregular sparse linear systems. We investigate the use of a novel hybrid preconditioner that combines the advantages of SPAI and PSAI with a more efficient and scalable approach to handle irregular sparse matrices.   We propose a new preconditioning framework that leverages the strengths of SPAI and PSAI, along with a novel sparse matrix factorization technique. Our approach involves a two-stage process first, we apply a sparse matrix factorization to the original matrix, followed by the application of SPAI or PSAI preconditioning to the resulting factorized matrix. We also introduce a novel optimization technique to adaptively select the most effective preconditioner for each matrix.   Our experimental results demonstrate that the proposed hybrid preconditioner can significantly improve the convergence of iterative linear solvers for large irregular sparse linear systems. We achieve better convergence rates and reduced computational costs compared to traditional preconditioning methods.   Our approach provides a novel solution to making SPAI and PSAI preconditioning effective for large irregular sparse linear systems. By combining the strengths of SPAI and PSAI with a more efficient and scalable approach, we can improve the performance of iterative linear solvers for a wide range of applications, including scientific simulations, machine learning, and data analysis.
label: machine

text:
We present the optical imaging polarimetric observations of comet C/2009
P1(Garradd) at three different phase angles e.g., 28.2$^\circ$, 28.1$^\circ$
and 21.6$^\circ$. The observations were carried out using IUCAA Faint Object
Spectrograph and Camera mounted on Cassegrain focus of the 2-m Telescope of
IGO, IUCAA, Pune in R$_{comet}$, R photometric bands, on 21 and 22 March 2012
and ARIES Imaging Polarimeter mounted on Cassegrain focus of the 1.04-m
Sampurnanand Telescope of ARIES, Nainital in R photometric band, on 23 May
2012. We show the presence of a jet activity in the rotational gradient treated
image of comet Garradd at phase angle 28.1$^\circ$. These jets are mainly
oriented towards the Sun and extended up to $\sim$ 5100 km from the cometary
photocenter. The antisolar extension of jet seems to be fainter, which is
extended up to $\sim$ 1800 km. It is found that the comet Garradd shows
negative polarization at phase angle 21.6$^\circ$. The degree of polarization
derived for Garradd is in good agreement with other comets at nearly similar
phase angles e.g., comets 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko, 22P/Kopff, 1P/Halley,
C/1990 K1 (Levy), 4P/Faye, and C/1995 O1 (Hale-Bopp) at phase angle $\sim$
28$^\circ$, and 47P/Ashbrook-Jackson at phase angle $\sim$ 21.6$^\circ$,
respectively. It is also found that the degree of polarization of dusty coma of
comet Garradd at phase angle $\sim$ 28$^\circ$ is high but, not as high as in
the case of comet Hale-Bopp.

text: The increasing complexity and size of attributed networks in various domains necessitate efficient methods for identifying top-k similar nodes based on a combination of attributes and structural properties. This paper addresses the challenge of diversified top-k similarity search within large attributed networks, providing a novel approach that balances traditional similarity metrics with diversity considerations. The objective is to enhance the relevance and quality of search results by ensuring a diverse yet similar set of nodes is retrieved. Our methodology introduces a hybrid model that integrates attribute-based similarity measures and network topology features with a diversification framework. This model employs a weighted scoring mechanism to rank nodes, ensuring that the diversity of returned results is maximized without compromising similarity. Extensive experiments were conducted on multiple large-scale attributed network datasets to evaluate the efficacy and efficiency of the proposed approach. Key findings indicate that our model outperforms existing techniques, achieving a higher diversification score while maintaining competitive retrieval accuracy and performance. The results suggest that incorporating diversification in the similarity search paradigm significantly enhances the utility of search results by providing a more comprehensive view of potential matches. In conclusion, this research demonstrates the viability of a diversified search strategy in large attributed networks, highlighting its potential to improve decision-making processes in applications ranging from social network analysis to biological network investigation.
label: machine

text:
A variety of observational evidence demonstrates that brown dwarfs exhibit
active atmospheric circulations. In this study we use a shallow-water model to
investigate the global atmospheric dynamics in the stratified layer overlying
the convective zone on these rapidly rotating objects. We show that the
existence and properties of the atmospheric circulation crucially depend on key
parameters including the energy injection rate and radiative timescale. Under
conditions of strong internal heat flux and weak radiative dissipation, a
banded flow pattern comprising east-west jet streams spontaneously emerges from
the interaction of atmospheric turbulence with the planetary rotation. In
contrast, when the internal heat flux is weak and/or radiative dissipation is
strong, turbulence injected into the atmosphere damps before it can
self-organize into jets, leading to a flow dominated by transient eddies and
isotropic turbulence instead. The simulation results are not very sensitive to
the form of the forcing. Based on the location of the transition between
jet-dominated and eddy-dominated regimes, we suggest that many brown dwarfs may
exhibit atmospheric circulations dominated by eddies and turbulence (rather
than jets) due to the strong radiative damping on these worlds, but a jet
structure is also possible under some realistic conditions. Our simulated light
curves capture important features from observed infrared lightcurves of brown
dwarfs, including amplitude variations of a few percent and shapes that
fluctuate between single-peak and multi-peak structures. More broadly, our work
shows that the shallow-water system provides a useful tool to illuminate
fundamental aspects of the dynamics on these worlds.
label: human

text:
WLAN localization has become an active research field recently. Due to the
wide WLAN deployment, WLAN localization provides ubiquitous coverage and adds
to the value of the wireless network by providing the location of its users
without using any additional hardware. However, WLAN localization systems
usually require constructing a radio map, which is a major barrier of WLAN
localization systems' deployment. The radio map stores information about the
signal strength from different signal strength streams at selected locations in
the site of interest. Typical construction of a radio map involves measurements
and calibrations making it a tedious and time-consuming operation. In this
paper, we present the AROMA system that automatically constructs accurate
active and passive radio maps for both device-based and device-free WLAN
localization systems. AROMA has three main goals: high accuracy, low
computational requirements, and minimum user overhead. To achieve high
accuracy, AROMA uses 3D ray tracing enhanced with the uniform theory of
diffraction (UTD) to model the electric field behavior and the human shadowing
effect. AROMA also automates a number of routine tasks, such as importing
building models and automatic sampling of the area of interest, to reduce the
user's overhead. Finally, AROMA uses a number of optimization techniques to
reduce the computational requirements. We present our system architecture and
describe the details of its different components that allow AROMA to achieve
its goals. We evaluate AROMA in two different testbeds. Our experiments show
that the predicted signal strength differs from the measurements by a maximum
average absolute error of 3.18 dBm achieving a maximum localization error of
2.44m for both the device-based and device-free cases.

text: We investigate the radiation mechanisms and physical properties of GeV-TeV BL Lac objects, a subclass of active galactic nuclei characterized by their intense emission across the electromagnetic spectrum. Our research addresses the challenge of understanding the underlying processes that govern their luminous output, particularly the emission of high-energy gamma rays. We employ a multi-frequency approach, integrating observational data from ground-based telescopes and satellite missions, coupled with advanced numerical modeling to simulate the particle acceleration mechanisms and radiation processes occurring within these systems.  Our results indicate that synchrotron emission and inverse Compton scattering are pivotal in explaining the observed spectral features of BL Lac objects in the GeV-TeV range. We find that the evolution of the jet composition and magnetic field intensity directly influences the radiation output, suggesting a complex interplay between relativistic jets and surrounding environments. Furthermore, we identify a correlation between spectral variability and intrinsic physical parameters, which has implications for understanding the emission mechanisms in these extreme astrophysical sources.  By situating our findings within the broader context of blazar research, we propose a refined model that accounts for the variability observed in multi-wavelength data, invoking a hybrid emission mechanism. This study enhances our comprehension of the physical processes at play in GeV-TeV BL Lac objects and sets the stage for future investigations aimed at unraveling the intricacies of extragalactic high-energy phenomena. Ultimately, our work contributes to the overarching goal of elucidating the nature of the universe's most energetic environments.

text: This study investigates the influence of multiple in-medium scattering processes on the momentum imbalance observed in reconstructed di-jet events. Through a series of Monte Carlo simulations, we explore various scenarios where jets are produced within dense hadronic environments, simulating conditions akin to those found in heavy-ion collisions at high energies. The simulations incorporate different types of in-medium scattering mechanisms, such as parton energy loss and jet quenching, which can lead to deviations from idealized vacuum predictions.  Our analysis reveals that these scattering processes significantly affect the momentum distribution of reconstructed di-jets, leading to increased momentum imbalances compared to predictions made under vacuum conditions. We employ detailed statistical methods to quantify these effects and identify the specific scattering processes responsible for the observed deviations. Key insights include the observation that higher-order scattering mechanisms contribute disproportionately to the momentum imbalance, particularly in regions of the phase space where the initial parton interactions are most pronounced.  The methodology involves extensive data analysis techniques to isolate and characterize the impact of each scattering process on the di-jet momentum distributions. Results demonstrate a clear correlation between the magnitude of momentum imbalance and the complexity of the in-medium scattering environment, highlighting the importance of accounting for these effects in high-energy physics experiments aimed at understanding the properties of strongly interacting matter. This work underscores the necessity of incorporating realistic hadronic interaction models when interpreting experimental data and provides a framework for future studies seeking to elucidate the underlying physics of jet production in extreme conditions.

text: We investigate the phenomenon of steady-state magnetic reconnection at a single three-dimensional (3D) magnetic null point, specifically addressing its implications for astrophysical and laboratory plasma systems. Our study aims to elucidate the underlying mechanisms governing reconnection dynamics and the resultant magnetic topology evolution. We employ a combination of numerical simulations and analytical methods to explore the stability and structure of the magnetic field in the vicinity of the null point, focusing on the formation of current sheets and associated energy release processes.   Our findings reveal that under certain conditions, the reconnection rate is significantly enhanced by the local geometry, leading to a rapid energization of plasma and a redistribution of magnetic energy in the system. We characterize the steady-state reconnection configuration and identify critical parameters influencing the process, including the strength of the applied magnetic field and the initial plasma conditions. Moreover, we demonstrate the relationship between the reconnection rate and plasma flows around the null point, providing insights into how these interactions can trigger larger-scale magnetic events.  We conclude that our results have profound implications for understanding energy conversion processes in natural astrophysical phenomena such as solar flares and magnetospheric dynamics. This work lays the foundation for future investigations into the broader implications of 3D magnetic reconnection and emphasizes the need for further exploration of 3D null points in various plasma contexts.

text:
A novel implementation for the skeletal reduction of large detailed reaction
mechanisms using the directed relation graph with error propagation and
sensitivity analysis (DRGEPSA) is developed and presented with examples for
three hydrocarbon components, n-heptane, iso-octane, and n-decane, relevant to
surrogate fuel development. DRGEPSA integrates two previously developed
methods, directed relation graph-aided sensitivity analysis (DRGASA) and
directed relation graph with error propagation (DRGEP), by first applying DRGEP
to efficiently remove many unimportant species prior to sensitivity analysis to
further remove unimportant species, producing an optimally small skeletal
mechanism for a given error limit. It is illustrated that the combination of
the DRGEP and DRGASA methods allows the DRGEPSA approach to overcome the
weaknesses of each, specifically that DRGEP cannot identify all unimportant
species and that DRGASA shields unimportant species from removal. Skeletal
mechanisms for n-heptane and iso-octane generated using the DRGEP, DRGASA, and
DRGEPSA methods are presented and compared to illustrate the improvement of
DRGEPSA. From a detailed reaction mechanism for n-alkanes covering n-octane to
n-hexadecane with 2115 species and 8157 reactions, two skeletal mechanisms for
n-decane generated using DRGEPSA, one covering a comprehensive range of
temperature, pressure, and equivalence ratio conditions for autoignition and
the other limited to high temperatures, are presented and validated. The
comprehensive skeletal mechanism consists of 202 species and 846 reactions and
the high-temperature skeletal mechanism consists of 51 species and 256
reactions. Both mechanisms are further demonstrated to well reproduce the
results of the detailed mechanism in perfectly-stirred reactor and laminar
flame simulations over a wide range of conditions.

text: This study investigates the problem of making bipartite graphs DM-irreducible, a fundamental concept in combinatorial optimization and network science. A bipartite graph is a graph whose vertices can be divided into two disjoint sets such that every edge connects a vertex in one set to a vertex in the other set. DM-irreducibility refers to the property of a bipartite graph that no proper subgraph can be a dominating set of the graph. In other words, a dominating set of a graph is a subset of vertices such that every vertex in the graph is either in the subset or adjacent to a vertex in the subset.  The objective of this research is to develop efficient algorithms for making bipartite graphs DM-irreducible. The existing literature on this topic is limited, and most existing algorithms have exponential time complexity. This study proposes a novel approach to solving this problem, which involves a combination of graph algorithms and machine learning techniques. The proposed algorithm, called DM-irreducibility algorithm, uses a genetic programming approach to search for a DM-irreducible dominating set in the bipartite graph.  The proposed algorithm is evaluated on a set of randomly generated bipartite graphs and compared with existing algorithms. The results show that the proposed algorithm has a significantly better time complexity than existing algorithms, making it a promising approach for large-scale bipartite graphs. The key findings of this study include the development of a novel algorithm for making bipartite graphs DM-irreducible and the evaluation of the algorithm's performance on a set of randomly generated graphs. The study also highlights the potential applications of this algorithm in various fields, including computer networks, logistics, and machine learning.

text:
Radio galaxy phenomenon is directly connected to mass accreting, spinning
supermassive black holes found in the active galactic nuclei (AGN). It is still
unclear how the collimated jets of relativistic plasma on hundreds to thousands
of kpc scale form, and why nearly always they are launched from the nuclei of
bulge dominated elliptical galaxies and not flat spirals. Here we present the
discovery of giant radio source J2345-0449 (z=0.0755), a clear and extremely
rare counter example where relativistic jets are ejected from a luminous and
massive spiral galaxy on scale of ~1.6 Mpc, the largest known so far. Extreme
physical properties observed for this bulgeless spiral host, such as its high
optical and infra-red luminosity, large dynamical mass, rapid disk rotation,
and episodic jet activity are possibly the results of its unusual formation
history, which has also assembled, via gas accretion from a disk, its central
black hole of mass >2 x 10^8 M_sun. The very high mid-IR luminosity of the
galaxy suggests that it is actively forming stars and still building a massive
disk. We argue that the launch of these powerful jets is facilitated by an
advection dominated, magnetized accretion flow at low Eddington rate onto this
unusually massive (for a bulgeless disk galaxy) and possibly fast-spinning
central black hole. Therefore, J2345-0449 is an extremely rare, unusual
galactic system whose properties challenge the standard paradigms for black
hole growth and formation of relativistic jets in disk galaxies. Thus, it
provides fundamental insight into accretion disk -- relativistic jet coupling
processes.

Modern computer vision is all about the possession of powerful image
representations. Deeper and deeper convolutional neural networks have been
built using larger and larger datasets and are made publicly available. A large
swath of computer vision scientists use these pre-trained networks with varying
degrees of successes in various tasks. Even though there is tremendous success
in copying these networks, the representational space is not learnt from the
target dataset in a traditional manner. One of the reasons for opting to use a
pre-trained network over a network learnt from scratch is that small datasets
provide less supervision and require meticulous regularization, smaller and
careful tweaking of learning rates to even achieve stable learning without
weight explosion. It is often the case that large deep networks are not
portable, which necessitates the ability to learn mid-sized networks from
scratch.
  In this article, we dive deeper into training these mid-sized networks on
small datasets from scratch by drawing additional supervision from a large
pre-trained network. Such learning also provides better generalization
accuracies than networks trained with common regularization techniques such as
l2, l1 and dropouts. We show that features learnt thus, are more general than
those learnt independently. We studied various characteristics of such networks
and found some interesting behaviors.

In recent years the global seismic scaling relations for the frequency of
maximum power and for the large frequency separation have caught the attention
of various fields of astrophysics. With the exquisite photometry of
\textit{Kepler}, the uncertainties in the seismic observables are small enough
to estimate masses and radii with a precision of only a few per cent. Even
though this seems to work quite well for main-sequence stars, there is
empirical evidence, mainly from studies of eclipsing binary systems, that the
seismic scaling relations overestimate the mass and radius of red giants by
about 15 and 5\%, respectively. Model-based corrections of the $\Delta\nu
-$scaling reduce the problem but do not solve it. We re-examine the global
oscillation parameters of the giants in the binary systems in order to
determine their seismic fundamental parameters and find them to agree with the
dynamic parameters from the literature if we adopt nonlinear scalings. We note
that a curvature and glitch corrected $\Delta\nu_\mathrm{cor}$ should be
preferred over a local or average values. We then compare the observed seismic
parameters of the cluster giants to those scaled from independent measurements
and find the same nonlinear behaviour as for the eclipsing binaries. Our final
proposed scaling relations are based on both samples and cover a broad range of
evolutionary stages from RGB to RC stars: $g/\sqrt{T_\mathrm{eff}} =
(\nu_\mathrm{max}/\nu_\mathrm{max,\odot})^{1.0075\pm0.0021}$ and
$\sqrt{\bar\rho} = (\Delta\nu_\mathrm{cor}/\Delta\nu_\mathrm{cor,\odot})[\eta -
(0.0085\pm0.0025) \log^2
(\Delta\nu_\mathrm{cor}/\Delta\nu_\mathrm{cor,\odot})]^{-1}$, where $g$,
$T_\mathrm{eff}$, and $\bar\rho$ are in solar units,
$\nu_\mathrm{max,\odot}=3140\pm5\mu$Hz and
$\Delta\nu_\mathrm{cor,\odot}=135.08\pm0.02\mu$Hz , and $\eta$ is equal to one
in case of RGB stars and $1.04\pm0.01$ for RC stars.

The hierarchical galaxy formation scenario in the Cold Dark Matter cosmogony
with a non-vanishing cosmological constant and geometrically flat space has
been very successful in explaining the large-scale distribution of galaxies.
However, there have been claims that the scenario predicts too many satellite
galaxies associated with massive galaxies compared to observations, called the
missing satellite galaxy problem. Isolated groups of galaxies hosted by
passively evolving massive early-type galaxies are ideal laboratories for
finding the missing physics in the current theory. Here we report from a deep
spectroscopic survey of such satellite systems that isolated massive early-type
galaxies with no recent star formation through wet mergers or accretion have
almost no satellite galaxies fainter than the r-band absolute magnitude of
about Mr =-14. If only early-type satellites are used, the cutoff is at
somewhat brighter magnitude of about Mr =-15. Such a cutoff has not been found
in other nearby satellite galaxy systems hosted by late-type galaxies or those
with merger features. Various physical properties of satellites depend strongly
on the host-centric distance. Our observation indicates that the satellite
galaxy luminosity function is largely determined by the interaction of
satellites with the environment provided by their host, which sheds light on
the missing satellite galaxy problem.

text:
The recent explosive growth in convolutional neural network (CNN) research
has produced a variety of new architectures for deep learning. One intriguing
new architecture is the bilinear CNN (B-CNN), which has shown dramatic
performance gains on certain fine-grained recognition problems [15]. We apply
this new CNN to the challenging new face recognition benchmark, the IARPA Janus
Benchmark A (IJB-A) [12]. It features faces from a large number of identities
in challenging real-world conditions. Because the face images were not
identified automatically using a computerized face detection system, it does
not have the bias inherent in such a database. We demonstrate the performance
of the B-CNN model beginning from an AlexNet-style network pre-trained on
ImageNet. We then show results for fine-tuning using a moderate-sized and
public external database, FaceScrub [17]. We also present results with
additional fine-tuning on the limited training data provided by the protocol.
In each case, the fine-tuned bilinear model shows substantial improvements over
the standard CNN. Finally, we demonstrate how a standard CNN pre-trained on a
large face database, the recently released VGG-Face model [20], can be
converted into a B-CNN without any additional feature training. This B-CNN
improves upon the CNN performance on the IJB-A benchmark, achieving 89.5%
rank-1 recall.

text: The coupling between polarization and vorticity in magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) systems has long been an intriguing topic in plasma physics. Two competing theories, thermodynamic and kinetic, have been proposed to explain this coupling. In the thermodynamic approach, vorticity generation is attributed to the conversion of magnetic energy into thermal energy via magnetic reconnection. In contrast, in the kinetic approach, vorticity is assumed to be produced by the plasma motion in the presence of a magnetic field. This study aims to explore the fundamental differences between these two approaches and investigate their implications on the dynamics of MHD systems. To accomplish this, we perform a comprehensive review of relevant literature and utilize numerical simulations to compare the outcomes of both approaches. We find that while the thermodynamic approach is well-suited for explaining the long-term behavior of MHD systems, it fails to capture the temporal evolution of the system. On the other hand, the kinetic approach is more effective in describing the transient behavior of MHD systems but lacks a clear physical mechanism to explain the vorticity generation. Our findings highlight the importance of understanding the underlying physics of polarization-vorticity coupling in MHD systems. We suggest that future research should focus on developing hybrid models that incorporate both thermodynamic and kinetic approaches to provide a more comprehensive understanding of this complex phenomenon. The implications of our results on space and astrophysical plasmas, fusion devices, and other relevant fields are significant and warrant further exploration.

text: The study investigates Majorana CP phases within the framework of bi-pair neutrino mixing and their implications for leptogenesis, a key process in explaining the baryon asymmetry of the universe. Understanding CP violation in the lepton sector, particularly through Majorana phases, is crucial for testing and refining models of neutrino masses and mixings. Our objective was to explore the potential links between Majorana CP phases and the generation of a lepton asymmetry that may contribute to baryogenesis via leptogenesis. We employed a theoretical analysis based on the seesaw mechanism, incorporating bi-pair mixing matrices to describe neutrino oscillations and emphasizing the role of CP violation in the decay processes of heavy right-handed neutrinos. By analyzing the parameter space allowed by current experimental data, our study derives conditions under which Majorana phases can significantly influence the CP asymmetry in heavy neutrino decays. Key findings indicate that, within certain regions of parameter space, Majorana CP phases can enhance leptogenesis efficiency, providing a viable pathway for the observed matter-antimatter asymmetry. Furthermore, our results suggest that future measurements of neutrino oscillation parameters will be instrumental in constraining these phases, enhancing the predictability of leptogenesis models. In conclusion, this research underscores the pivotal role of Majorana CP phases in the viable incorporation of neutrino physics into models of early-universe baryogenesis, highlighting the need for further experimental and theoretical investigations to confirm the hypothesized connections.

text:
The Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) is widely recognized as the most
important block cipher in common use nowadays. This high assurance in AES is
given by its resistance to ten years of extensive cryptanalysis, that has shown
no weakness, not even any deviation from the statistical behaviour expected
from a random permutation. Only reduced versions of the ciphers have been
broken, but they are not usually implemented. In this paper we build a
distinguishing attack on the AES, exploiting the properties of a novel cipher
embedding. With our attack we give some statistical evidence that the set of
AES-$128$ encryptions acts on the message space in a way significantly
different than that of the set of random permutations acting on the same space.
While we feel that more computational experiments by independent third parties
are needed in order to validate our statistical results, we show that the
non-random behaviour is the same as we would predict using the property of our
embedding. Indeed, the embedding lowers the nonlinearity of the AES rounds and
therefore the AES encryptions tend, on average, to keep low the rank of
low-rank matrices constructed in the large space. Our attack needs $2^{23}$
plaintext-ciphertext pairs and costs the equivalent of $2^{48}$ encryptions.
  We expect our attack to work also for AES-$192$ and AES-$256$, as confirmed
by preliminary experiments.

text:
Millimeter wave (mmWave) communication with large array gains is a key
ingredient of next generation (5G) wireless networks. Effective communication
in mmWaves usually depends on the knowledge of the channel. We refer to the
problem of finding a narrow beam pair at the transmitter and at the receiver,
yielding high Signal to Noise Ratio (SNR) as Beam Alignment (BA). Prior BA
schemes typically considered deterministic channels, where the instantaneous
channel coefficients are assumed to stay constant for a long time. In this
paper, in contrast, we propose a time-domain BA scheme for wideband mmWave
systems, where the channel is characterized by multi-path components, different
delays, Angle-of-Arrivals/Angle-of-Departures (AoAs/AoDs), and Doppler shifts.
In our proposed scheme, the Base Station (BS) probes the channel in the
downlink by some sequences with good autocorrelation property (e.g.,
Pseudo-Noise (PN) sequences), letting each user estimate its best AoA-AoD that
connects the user to the BS with two-sided high beamforming gain. We leverage
the sparse nature of mmWaves in the AoA-AoD-time domain, and formulate the BA
problem as a Compressed Sensing (CS) of a non-negative sparse vector. We use
the recently developed Non-Negative Least Squares (NNLS) technique to
efficiently find the strongest path connecting the BS and each user. Simulation
results show that the proposed scheme outperforms its counterpart in terms of
the training overhead and robustness to fast channel variations.

text: Textile composites, due to their unique properties, are increasingly used in aerospace and automotive industries. However, their quasibrittle nature poses challenges in the analysis and design of such structures. Spectral Stiffness Microplane Model (SSMM) is an effective tool to estimate the mechanical behavior of orthotropic quasibrittle materials. In this study, the applicability of the SSMM to textile composites is investigated. For this purpose, the unidirectional carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP) fabrics were prepared and tested under tensile loading. The microplane stiffness matrices were derived based on the experimental data. These matrices were employed in the SSMM to predict the biaxial response of the CFRP composites. The SSMM predictions were compared to the experimental results and found to be in good agreement. The damage evolution was also modeled using the SSMM, which effectively predicted the onset and progression of the matrix and fiber damages. The SSMM provided valuable insights into the complex mechanical behavior of textile composites and can be useful in the analysis and design of such structures in various industries.
