text: In this work, we investigate the convexity properties of the extended K-energy functional and the asymptotic behaviour of weak solutions of the Calabi flow over complex manifolds. This study addresses the ongoing challenge of understanding the stability and convergence properties of geometric flows in the context of Kähler geometry. We utilize a variational approach to explore the functional's convexity with respect to weak metrics, offering a robust framework for analyzing the critical points and minimizing sequences. Through this framework, we establish new results that confirm the extended K-energy's convexity along geodesic rays in the space of Kähler potentials. Our methodology involves the application of energy techniques and a careful analysis of the functional's derivative properties in weak settings. To elucidate the large-time behaviour of the weak Calabi flow, we develop novel estimates demonstrating uniform bounds for the solution. These estimates ensure that the flow converges to extremal metrics under appropriate initial conditions. Our results significantly enhance the understanding of the global dynamical properties of the Calabi flow, particularly highlighting the influence of the extended K-energy’s convexity on long-term stability. This research contributes to the broader endeavour of elucidating the geometric and analytic structure of moduli spaces of complex structures endowed with extremal metrics. Our findings suggest potential applications in related fields, including the study of geometric stability and the classification of complex manifolds, thus opening avenues for future research exploring deeper interactions between complex differential geometry and algebraic geometry.

text: In this study, we investigate the universal transport signatures of Majorana fermions in superconductor-Luttinger liquid (SL) junctions, aiming to elucidate their unique properties and potential applications. We find that the presence of Majorana fermions leads to distinctive features in the zero-bias conductance peak, characterized by a finite width and non-monotonic behavior as a function of temperature and chemical potential. The key methodology involves solving the Bogoliubov-de Gennes equations within the framework of Luttinger liquid theory, coupled with Kubo formulae for transport calculations. Our results highlight the robustness of these signatures, which can be exploited for the development of topological quantum computing devices and other advanced quantum technologies. Notably, our findings corroborate with existing experimental observations and suggest a universal approach to detect Majorana fermions in such systems.

JHKs photometry is presented from a three-year survey of the central regions
of the Local Group dwarf irregular galaxy IC1613. The morphologies of the
colour-magnitude and colour-colour diagrams are discussed with particular
reference to the supergiants and M- and C-type asymptotic giant branch (AGB)
stars. Mean JHKs magnitudes, amplitudes and periods are given for five O-rich
and nine C-rich Mira variables for which bolometric magnitudes are also
estimated. A distance of 750 kpc ($(m-M)_0=24.37\pm 0.08$ mag) is derived for
IC1613 by fitting a period-luminosity relation to the C-rich Miras. This is in
agreement with values from the literature. The AGB stars exhibit a range of
ages. A comparison with theoretical isochrones suggests that four luminous
O-rich Miras are as young as $2\times 10^8$ yrs. One of these has a lithium
absorption line in its spectrum, demonstrating that it is undergoing hot bottom
burning (HBB). This supports the idea that HBB is the cause of the high
luminosity of these AGB stars, which puts them above the fundamental
period-luminosity (PL) relation. Further studies of similar stars, selected
from their positions in the PL diagram, could provide insight into HBB. A much
fainter, presumed O-rich, Mira is similar to those found in Galactic globular
clusters. The C Miras are of intermediate age.
  The O-rich variables are not all recognized as O-rich, or even as AGB stars,
on the basis of their J-Ks colour. It is important to appreciate this when
using near-infrared surveys to classify AGB stars in more distant galaxies.

text: The Cherenkov Telescope Array (CTA) represents the next generation of ground-based observatories for detecting gamma rays. The objective is to evaluate CTA's capacity to detect celestial gamma-ray sources with unprecedented precision. These were analyzed using robust statistical methods and advanced data reconstruction algorithms to determine the system's sensitivity and resolution across different energy domains. Key findings illustrate that the CTA achieves significantly enhanced sensitivity, particularly at lower energies, due to its advanced array configurations and technology. Results from simulated Crab observations demonstrate a substantial improvement in flux measurements, offering deeper insights into the nebula's emission mechanisms. The analysis confirms that the CTA can conduct detailed spectral studies and detect new sources with lower flux thresholds. In conclusion, the CTA is poised to become a leading instrument in gamma-ray astronomy, providing crucial data for exploring astrophysical phenomena and contributing to the broader field of high-energy astrophysics. text: The luminosity of horizontal branch (HB) stars in globular clusters is a crucial parameter for understanding stellar evolution and the impact of metallicity on stellar populations. Our key findings indicate a systematic correlation between HB luminosity and metallicity, with higher metallicity globular clusters exhibiting brighter HB stars. This correlation is further constrained by considering the age and evolutionary phase of the clusters. Our results contribute to the ongoing discussion on the influence of metallicity in shaping the properties of stellar populations and reinforce the need for further studies on individual cluster characteristics. text: This research characterizes the youngest protostars detected by the Herschel Space Observatory, focusing on molecular outflows observed across the millimeter and far-infrared wavelengths. text: We investigate the radiative and collisional processes in translationally cold samples of hydrogen Rydberg atoms utilizing an electrostatic trap. Our work addresses the challenge of understanding the interactions governing the behavior of Rydberg atoms at low temperatures, which can be critical for applications in quantum simulations and information processing. Our results demonstrate that the doped Rydberg atoms experience significant modifications in their decay rates and collisional behaviors when confined in an electrostatic trap. We observe an increase in the lifetimes of Rydberg states due to suppression of electric dipole transitions at low kinetic energies, highlighting a distinctive regime of collisional repulsion that emerges from the dipole interactions among Rydberg atoms.  Furthermore, we provide detailed models based on quantum mechanical principles to elucidate the mechanisms underlying these processes. Our findings not only enhance the understanding of Rydberg atom interactions but also establish a foundation for future research into many-body quantum systems. text: This study explores the application of Gaussian approximations to model single-particle correlations within Lennard-Jones and nanoparticle fluid systems over picosecond timescales. These simulations are then analyzed to extract single-particle correlation functions. The Gaussian approximation is applied to these functions, allowing us to derive analytical expressions that describe the correlation behavior.  The results indicate that the Gaussian approximation significantly improves the accuracy of describing short-time correlations compared to classical approaches, particularly for systems where thermal fluctuations dominate. Key findings include the identification of characteristic time scales and the elucidation of how particle interactions influence these timescales. Modern latency-critical online services often rely on composing results from
a large number of server components. Hence the tail latency (e.g. the 99th
percentile of response time), rather than the average, of these components
determines the overall service performance. When hosted on a cloud environment,
the components of a service typically co-locate with short batch jobs to
increase machine utilizations, and share and contend resources such as caches
and I/O bandwidths with them. The highly dynamic nature of batch jobs in terms
of their workload types and input sizes causes continuously changing
performance interference to individual components, hence leading to their
latency variability and high tail latency. However, existing techniques either
ignore such fine-grained component latency variability when managing service
performance, or rely on executing redundant requests to reduce the tail
latency, which adversely deteriorate the service performance when load gets
heavier. In this paper, we propose PCS, a predictive and component-level
scheduling framework to reduce tail latency for large-scale, parallel online
services. It uses an analytical performance model to simultaneously predict the
component latency and the overall service performance on different nodes. Based
on the predicted performance, the scheduler identifies straggling components
and conducts near-optimal component-node allocations to adapt to the changing
performance interferences from batch jobs. We demonstrate that, using realistic
workloads, the proposed scheduler reduces the component tail latency by an
average of 67.05\% and the average overall service latency by 64.16\% compared
with the state-of-the-art techniques on reducing tail latency.

Large-scale magnetic fields are key ingredients of magnetically driven disk
accretion. We study how large-scale poloidal fields evolve in accretion disks,
with the primary aim of quantifying the viability of magnetic accretion
mechanisms in protoplanetary disks. We employ a kinematic mean-field model for
poloidal field transport and focus on steady states where inward advection of a
field balances with outward diffusion due to effective resistivities. We
analytically derive the steady-state radial distribution of poloidal fields in
highly conducting accretion disks. The analytic solution reveals an upper limit
on the strength of large-scale vertical fields attainable in steady states. Any
excess poloidal field will be diffused away within a finite time, and we
demonstrate this with time-dependent numerical calculations of the mean-field
equations. We apply this upper limit to large-scale vertical fields threading
protoplanetary disks. We find that the maximum attainable strength is about 0.1
G at 1 AU, and about 1 mG at 10 AU from the central star. When combined with
recent magnetic accretion models, the maximum field strength translates into
the maximum steady-state accretion rate of $\sim 10^{-7} M_\odot {\rm
yr}^{-1}$, in agreement with observations. We also find that the maximum field
strength is ~ 1 kG at the surface of the central star provided that the disk
extends down to the stellar surface. This implies that any excess stellar
poloidal field of strength >~ kG can be transported to the surrounding disk.
This might in part resolve the magnetic flux problem in star formation.

The long-term optical and infrared color variability of blazars has been
investigated with the SMARTS monitoring data. The sample in this study consists
of 49 flat spectrum radio quasars and 22 BL Lac objects. The fractional
variability amplitudes of each source have been calculated in both optical R
band and infrared J band. Overall, the variability amplitudes of FSRQs are
larger than those of BL Lac objects. The results also suggest that the
variability amplitude of most FSRQs is larger at lower energy band (J band)
than at higher one (R band), while the variability amplitude of BL Lacs are
larger at higher energy band. Two types of blazars both display color variation
along with the variability in brightness. However, they show different
variation behaviors in general. With the whole data set, 35 FSRQs exhibit
redder-when-brighter trends, and 11 FSRQs exhibit opposite trends; 11 BL Lacs
follow bluer-when-brighter trends, and 7 BL Lacs follow opposite trends. The
examination in detail shows that there are 10 blazars showing
redder-when-brighter trend in their low state, and bluer-when-brighter or
stable-when-brighter trends in their high state. Some more complicated color
behaviors have also been detected in several blazars. The non-thermal jet
emission and the thermal emission from the accretion disc are employed to
explain the observed color behaviors.

Recently it has been suggested that the fragmentation boundary in Smoothed
Particle Hydrodynamic (SPH) and FARGO simulations of self-gravitating accretion
discs with beta-cooling do not converge as resolution is increased.
Furthermore, this recent work suggests that by carefully optimising the
artificial viscosity parameters in these codes it can be shown that
fragmentation may occur for much longer cooling times than earlier work
suggests. If correct, this result is intriguing as it suggests that gas giant
planets could form, via direct gravitational collapse, reasonably close to
their parent stars. This result is, however, slightly surprising and there have
been a number of recent studies suggesting that the result is likely an
indication of a numerical problem with the simulations. One suggestion, in
particular, is that the SPH results are influenced by the manner in which the
cooling is implemented. We extend this work here and show that if the cooling
is implemented in a manner that removes a known numerical artefact in the shock
regions, the fragmentation boundary converges to a value consistent with
earlier work and that fragmentation is unlikely for the long cooling times
suggested by this recent work. We also investigate the optimisation of the
artificial viscosity parameters and show that the values that appear optimal
are likely introducing numerical problems in both the SPH and FARGO
simulations. We therefore conclude that earlier predictions for the cooling
times required for fragmentation are likely correct and that, as suggested by
this earlier work, fragmentation cannot occur in the inner parts (r < 50 au) of
typical protostellar discs.

text: We investigated the formation and evolution of dissipative standing shock waves around black holes, a phenomenon predicted by recent theoretical models. Through numerical simulations, we successfully reproduced the characteristic features of these shock waves, including the formation of a bow shock, a contact discontinuity, and a post-shock region. Our results indicate that the dissipation of energy in the post-shock region is primarily due to the interaction between the shock wave and the surrounding accretion disk.  We employed a 2D, axisymmetric numerical code to simulate the interaction between a black hole and a surrounding accretion disk, with the shock wave propagating through the disk. The simulations revealed that the bow shock and contact discontinuity are formed due to the non-linear interaction between the shock wave and the disk, leading to a significant increase in the accretion rate around the black hole. The post-shock region exhibits a complex structure, with multiple layers of gas and a high-temperature plasma.  Our findings suggest that dissipative standing shock waves around black holes play a crucial role in regulating the accretion rate and the energy output of these objects. We also demonstrate that the characteristics of these shock waves can be used to constrain models of black hole accretion and to better understand the physics of these systems.

text: We develop a variational formulation of electrostatics in a medium with spatially varying dielectric permittivity, addressing the limitations of traditional approaches by incorporating the non-uniform dielectric properties. Our formulation is based on the minimization of a variational functional that accounts for the electrostatic potential, the dielectric displacement, and the boundary conditions. We derive the Euler-Lagrange equations for the potential and the displacement, and show that they lead to a system of partial differential equations that describe the electrostatic behavior of the medium.  We demonstrate the applicability of our formulation by solving a series of test problems, including a homogeneous medium, a medium with a spatially varying dielectric permittivity, and a medium with a discontinuity in the dielectric properties. Our results show that the variational formulation accurately captures the electrostatic behavior of the medium, including the effects of spatially varying dielectric properties and discontinuities.  We also compare our results with those obtained using traditional approaches, such as the Poisson-Boltzmann equation and the finite element method. Our results show that the variational formulation provides a more accurate and robust solution, especially in cases where the dielectric properties vary significantly. Our formulation also allows for the incorporation of additional effects, such as non-uniform charge distributions and surface charge densities, which are not accounted for by traditional approaches.

Landmark-based human action recognition in videos is a challenging task in
computer vision. One key step is to design a generic approach that generates
discriminative features for the spatial structure and temporal dynamics. To
this end, we regard the evolving landmark data as a high-dimensional path and
apply non-linear path signature techniques to provide an expressive, robust,
non-linear, and interpretable representation for the sequential events. We do
not extract signature features from the raw path, rather we propose path
disintegrations and path transformations as preprocessing steps. Path
disintegrations turn a high-dimensional path linearly into a collection of
lower-dimensional paths; some of these paths are in pose space while others are
defined over a multiscale collection of temporal intervals. Path
transformations decorate the paths with additional coordinates in standard ways
to allow the truncated signatures of transformed paths to expose additional
features. For spatial representation, we apply the signature transform to
vectorize the paths that arise out of pose disintegration, and for temporal
representation, we apply it again to describe this evolving vectorization.
Finally, all the features are collected together to constitute the input vector
of a linear single-hidden-layer fully-connected network for classification.
Experimental results on four datasets demonstrated that the proposed feature
set with only a linear shallow network and Dropconnect is effective and
achieves comparable state-of-the-art results to the advanced deep networks, and
meanwhile, is capable of interpretation.

text: ExoData is an open-source Python package designed to manage and analyze large exoplanet catalog data. This tool offers a comprehensive solution to astronomers and researchers seeking to explore and understand exoplanet properties.   The discovery of exoplanets has accelerated at an unprecedented rate, resulting in vast catalogues of data. Handling and analyzing these data require efficient, adaptable, and powerful tools.   ExoData's primary objective is to facilitate data processing, manipulation, and visualization for exoplanet catalogues, making it an indispensable asset for the exoplanet research community.   ExoData imports and integrates data from various sources, including NASA's Exoplanet Archive and the Open Exoplanet Catalogue. It provides functionalities such as data cleaning, statistical analysis, data merging, and data querying. Moreover, it allows for customized visualization of exoplanet properties using popular data visualization libraries like Matplotlib and Seaborn.   The implementation of ExoData has shown significant improvements in handling large datasets, reducing processing time and memory consumption. It also allows users to perform complex analyses, enabling them to derive new insights from existing data.   ExoData offers a robust, versatile, and user-friendly solution for managing and analyzing large exoplanet catalog data. It is an essential tool for astronomers, researchers, and data scientists working in the field of exoplanet research. Its open-source nature encourages collaboration and community-driven development, further strengthening its position in the exoplanet research landscape.

We review the collectivity and the suppression pattern of charmed mesons -
produced in proton-nucleus and nucleus-nucleus collisions at SPS (158 AGeV) and
RHIC energies (21 ATeV) - in comparison to dynamical and thermal models. In
particular, we examine the charmonium `melting' and the `comover dissociation'
scenarios - implemented in a microscopic transport approach - in comparison to
the available data from the SPS and RHIC. The analysis shows that the dynamics
of c, c-bar quarks at RHIC are dominated by partonic or `pre-hadronic'
interactions in the strongly coupled plasma stage. Both the `charmonium
melting' and the hadronic `comover absorption and recreation model' are found,
however, to be compatible with the experimental observation at SPS energies;
the experimental ratio of Psi'/J/Psi versus centrality clearly favors the
`hadronic comover' scenario. We find that the collective flow of charm in the
purely hadronic Hadron-String Dynamics (HSD) transport appears compatible with
the data at SPS energies, but substantially underestimates the data at top RHIC
energies. Thus, the large elliptic flow v2 of D-mesons and the low R_AA(p_T) of
J/Psi seen experimentally have to be attributed to early interactions of
non-hadronic degrees of freedom. Simultaneously, we observe that non-hadronic
interactions are mandatory in order to describe the narrowing of the J/Psi
rapidity distribution from pp to central Au+Au collisions at the top RHIC
energy. We demonstrate additionally that the strong quenching of low-pT J/Psi's
in central Au+Au collisions indicates that a large fraction of final J/Psi
mesons is created by a coalescence mechanism close to the phase boundary.
Throughout this review we, furthermore, provide predictions for charm
observables from Au+Au collisions at FAIR energies of 25-35 AGeV.

In this paper, we study the geometry of a connected oriented cmc Riemannian
hypersurface $M$ of a semi-Riemannian group $G$ of Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$
and index 0 or 1. If $G$ is Riemannian and $M$ is compact and transversal to an
element of $\mathfrak g$, we show that it is a lateral class of a closed
embedded Lie subgroup of $G$; we also do this if $G$ is Lorentzian, provided
$M$ has sufficiently large mean curvature. If $G$ is Riemannian semisimple and
$M$ is compact, we prove that $M$ has degenerate Gauss map and minimal relative
nullity at least 1. We also extend the above results to the case where $M$ is
complete and noncompact. For a Riemannian $G$, we show that a minimal $M$ is
either transversal to an element of $\mathfrak g$, hence stable, or has
degenerate Gauss map and minimal relative nullity at least 1; for $M$ cmc and
transversal to an element of $\mathfrak g$, if we ask the immersion to be
proper and have bounded second fundamental form, then $M$ is also a lateral
class of a closed embedded Lie subgroup of $G$, provided a certain growing
condition on the size of the corresponding Gauss map is satisfied. Finally, for
a Lorentzian group $G$, with sectional curvatures bounded from above on
Lorentzian planes, we extend a result of Y. Xin, proving that a complete $M$ is
totally umbilical, provided it is transversal to a timelike element of
$\mathfrak g$, has large enough mean curvature and bounded hyperbolic Gauss
map.

We present the results of a Suzaku observation of Abell 1674, an optically
very rich (richness class 3) cluster cataloged as z = 0.1066. We discover the
He-like Fe K-shell line from the central region for the first time, and find
that the X-ray spectrum yields a high redshift of 0.215^{+0.007}_{-0.006}. On
the other hand, the spectrum of the southwestern region is fitted with a
redshift of 0.11 \pm 0.02 by the He-like Fe L-shell lines, consistent with the
optically determined value. The gas temperature, metal abundance, and core
radius of the X-ray emission in the central region are 3.8 \pm 0.2 keV, 0.20
\pm 0.05 Z_solar and 450 \pm 40 kpc, respectively, while those in the
southwestern region are 2.0 \pm 0.2 keV, 0.41^{+0.17}_{-0.13} Z_solar and
220^{+90}_{-70} kpc, respectively. These parameters are typical for clusters.
We thus conclude that Abell 1674 consists of two independent clusters, A1674-C
at z ~0.22 and A1674-SW at z ~0.11, overlapping along the line of sight. The
X-ray luminosities of A1674-C within r = 2 Mpc is 15.9 \pm 0.6 \times 10^{43}
erg s^{-1} in the 0.1-2.4 keV energy band, while that for A1674-SW is 1.25 \pm
0.07 \times 10^{43} erg s^{-1}. Both are consistent with those expected from
the L-T relation of clusters within a factor of 2. This is another support for
our conclusion.

text: In this study, we investigate the Luminosity Function (LF) and stellar Mass-to-Light ratio (\(M/L\)) of the massive globular cluster NGC2419. Our research aims to address the discrepancies in previous studies regarding the LF and \(M/L\) values of this particular cluster. Utilizing deep photometric data obtained from advanced telescopes, we analyze the distribution of luminosities of individual stars within NGC2419 to construct its LF. By comparing our LF results with theoretical models, we derive the stellar \(M/L\) ratio for NGC2419.  Our findings reveal a unique LF for NGC2419, suggesting a different stellar distribution compared to other globular clusters. The derived \(M/L\) ratio indicates a significant mass discrepancy within the cluster, challenging existing mass estimation methods. This discrepancy may be attributed to the presence of dark matter or the peculiar dynamical history of NGC2419. Our study unveils the importance of accurate LF and \(M/L\) determinations for understanding the internal dynamics and mass content of massive globular clusters. The methodology employed in this research can be extended to study other globular clusters and provide valuable insights into their stellar populations and mass-to-light characteristics.

Brightest Cluster Galaxies (BCGs) are believed to have assembled most of
their stars early in time and, therefore, should be passively evolving at low
redshifts and appear "red-and-dead." However, there have been reports that a
minority of low-redshift BCGs still have ongoing star formation rates (SFR) of
a few to even $\sim$100 $M_\odot/yr$. Such BCGs are found in "cool-core" ("CC")
clusters, and their star formation is thought to be fueled by "cooling flow."
To further investigate the implications of low-redshift, star-forming BCGs, we
perform a systematic search using the 22$\mu$m data ("W4" band) from the
Wide-field Infrared Survey Explorer (WISE) on the GMBCG catalog, which contains
55,424 BCGs at $0.1\lesssim z\lesssim 0.55$ identified in the Sloan Digital Sky
Survey (SDSS). Our sample consists of 389 BCGs that are bright in W4
("W4BCGs"), most being brighter than 5 mJy. While some ($\lesssim 20\%$) might
host AGN, most W4BCGs should owe their strong mid-IR emissions to
dust-enshrouded star formation. Their median total IR luminosity ($L_{IR}$) is
$5\times10^{11} L_{\odot}$ (SFR $\sim$50 $M_{\odot}/yr)$, and 27\% of the whole
sample has $L_{IR}>10^{12} L_{\odot}$ (SFR $>$100 $M_{\odot}/yr$). Using ten
W4BCGs that have Chandra X-ray data, we show that seven of them are possibly in
CC clusters. However, in most cases (five out of seven) the mass deposition
rate cannot account for the observed SFR. This casts doubt to the idea that
cooling flows are the cause of the star formation in non-quiescent BCGs.

The ultimate fates of binary companions to stars (including whether the
companion survives and the final orbit of the binary) are of interest in light
of an increasing number of recently discovered, low-mass companions to white
dwarfs (WDs). In this Letter, we study the evolution of a two-body system
wherein the orbit adjusts due to structural changes in the primary, dissipation
of orbital energy via tides, and mass loss during the giant phases; previous
studies have not incorporated changes in the primary's spin. For companions
ranging from Jupiter's mass to ~0.3 Msun and primaries ranging from 1-3 Msun,
we determine the minimum initial semimajor axis required for the companion to
avoid engulfment by the primary during post-main-sequence evolution, and
highlight the implications for the ultimate survival of the known exoplanets.
We present regions in secondary mass and orbital period space where an engulfed
companion might be expected to survive the common envelope phase (CEP), and
compare with known M dwarf+WD short-period binaries. Finally, we note that
engulfed Earth-like planets cannot survive a CEP. Detection of a
first-generation terrestrial planet in the white dwarf habitable zone requires
scattering from a several-AU orbit to a high-eccentricity orbit (with a
periastron of ~Rsun) from which it is damped into a circular orbit via tidal
friction, possibly rendering it an uninhabitable, charred ember.

text:
Mars is the only planet, other than Earth, for which there are several
evidences that liquid water was abundant at the surface. Among them, one of the
best evidence is that the ancient terrains of Mars are covered with fluvial and
lacustrine features such as valley networks, longitudinal valleys and basin
lakes. In addition, spectroscopic data have shown the widespread presence of
aqueous alteration minerals on the Martian surface, including clays composed by
phyllosilicates and hydrated salts. The main subject of my PhD is the study of
these specific features (such as valley networks and paleolakes) on Mars
surface, both from the geological and spectroscopic point of view through
mapping, sediment transport modelling and CRISM spectra analyses. There are, in
fact, no doubts that these structures were carved by liquid water, but several
questions remain about the mechanisms of their formation and the climatic
conditions under which this formation occurred. In this context, the study of
these structures along with the identification of hydrated minerals, are a key
in the investigation of the past climatic conditions of the planet which can
have, in turn, important astrobiological implications. I updated previous
global maps of Martian valleys using a new photomosaic of the Martian surface
and data at higher resolution with respect to those used in the previous works.
Furthermore, I selected a subset of the mapped valleys which includes 63 large
fluvial systems and evaluated their formation timescales on the basis of
sediment transport modelling. In addition, analyses of CRISM spectral data were
performed on a sample of open/closed basin lakes (associated with the mapped
valleys) detecting the possible presence of hydrated minerals, in particular
(Fe/Mg-smectite), sometimes in association with mafic materials (olivine).

text: We report the discovery of a high-frequency X-ray quasi-periodic oscillation (QPO) and iron K alpha reverberation in the active galaxy MS 2254.9-3712. Through a combination of simultaneous X-ray and optical observations, we detected a ~2 hour periodic signal in the X-ray spectrum, corresponding to a QPO with a frequency of 0.73 Hz. This frequency is significantly higher than previously reported QPOs in active galaxies, indicating a potentially new class of oscillators. Furthermore, we observed a strong correlation between the X-ray and optical light curves, suggesting a reverberation effect where the X-ray emission is modulated by the optical disk. The iron K alpha line, which is typically associated with the hot accretion disk, shows a significant increase in intensity during the QPO period, indicating a possible connection between the QPO and the accretion process. Our results suggest that the QPO is likely powered by the gravitational interaction between the accretion disk and the central black hole, and that the reverberation effect is a result of the disk's response to the QPO. The discovery of this high-frequency QPO and iron K alpha reverberation in MS 2254.9-3712 provides new insights into the physics of active galactic nuclei and the behavior of accretion disks in these systems.

text: This study investigates the information content encoded within the weak-charge form factor, a crucial component in the description of hadronic processes. Our approach involves a detailed analysis of the form factor's behavior across various energy scales, leveraging advanced theoretical frameworks such as Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) and lattice QCD simulations. The results reveal intricate patterns that correspond to specific quantum numbers and spin configurations, providing insights into the underlying dynamics of hadron interactions. Challenges encountered include the complexity of extracting meaningful information from the data due to the presence of non-perturbative effects and discretization errors in lattice calculations. To address these issues, we employed sophisticated techniques for data cleaning and regularization. Key methodologies include the application of dispersion relations to infer missing information and machine learning algorithms to enhance the precision of predictions. Overall, our findings contribute significantly to the understanding of hadronic structure and the development of more accurate models for describing strong interaction processes.

text: In this study, we investigate the analysis of Type-II hybrid censored competing risks data. The problem we address is the complexity involved in analyzing survival data when facing both competing risks and censoring, specifically Type-II hybrid censoring. Our goal is to develop a methodology that can effectively handle this type of data to provide reliable results in survival analysis.   Our research involved the development of a novel approach that combines the concepts of competing risks and Type-II hybrid censoring. We utilized statistical survival analysis techniques along with competing risks models to account for the presence of multiple failure types. Additionally, we incorporated Type-II hybrid censoring mechanisms to address the potential biases introduced by this censoring scheme.   Through the application of our proposed methodology on simulated datasets and real-world examples, we were able to demonstrate its effectiveness in handling Type-II hybrid censored competing risks data. The results indicate that our approach provides accurate estimates of survival probabilities and hazard functions, thus offering a robust solution to the challenges posed by this complex type of data. This study contributes to the advancement of survival analysis methods, particularly in scenarios involving competing risks and Type-II hybrid censoring, and offers valuable insights for researchers and practitioners in various fields.

The measurement of di-Higgs physics can provide crucial information on
electroweak phase transition in the early Universe and significant clues on new
physics coupling with the Higgs field directly. This measurement has been
suggested to be pursued mainly via the $pp \to hh$ production. In this letter,
we propose a new strategy to do that, i.e., via the $pp \to t \bar t hh $
production. Because of its positive correlation with the rescaled tri-Higgs
coupling $\frac{\lambda}{\lambda_{\rm SM}}$ (in comparison to a negative one
for the $pp \to hh$ production) in the neighborhood of
$\frac{\lambda}{\lambda_{\rm SM}} \sim 1$, the $pp \to t\bar t hh$ production
complements the $pp \to hh$ one in measuring di-Higgs physics, particularly for
$\frac{\lambda}{\lambda_{\rm SM}}>1$, at both the High Luminosity LHC (HL-LHC)
and a next-generation $pp$-collider. As an illustration, we work on the process
$pp\to t\bar thh \to t\bar t b\bar b b\bar b$. We show that a statistical
significance of $> 2.0 \sigma$ at the HL-LHC, comparable to that of the $pp \to
hh \to b\bar b \gamma\gamma$ channel, and a statistical significance of $\sim 5
\sigma$ at a 100 TeV $pp$-collider, with 3000 fb$^{-1}$ of data, are achievable
in searching for the di-Higgs production with $\frac{\lambda}{\lambda_{\rm SM}}
= 1$.

text: This work addresses the critical challenge of minimizing user traffic consumption within the realm of guaranteed advertising, a growing concern in digital marketing and user experience. We propose an efficient delivery policy that optimally allocates advertising resources while accommodating varying user connectivity conditions and preferences. Our methodology employs a dual-phase approach first, we analyze the traffic implications of different advertising strategies through simulations that incorporate real-world user behavior data; second, we implement a dynamic optimization framework that adjusts the delivery of advertisements based on real-time traffic metrics.   Our results demonstrate a significant reduction in overall user traffic without compromising the effectiveness of advertising campaigns. Specifically, we achieve a 30% decrease in data consumption while maintaining user engagement levels comparable to traditional delivery methods. Through extensive testing in diverse environments, we identify key factors affecting traffic consumption, including ad format, delivery time, and user demographics.  We find that personalized ad delivery not only enhances user satisfaction but also optimizes bandwidth utilization effectively. This research contributes to the growing body of knowledge surrounding intelligent advertising practices, offering practical insights for advertisers seeking to balance engagement with efficient resource use. Our findings suggest that with the implementation of our proposed delivery policy, stakeholders can achieve a more sustainable advertising model that respects user data limits while maximizing business outcomes.

text: We investigated the compositional diversity in the atmospheres of hot Neptunes, with a focus on the gas giant planet GJ 436b. Through a combination of spectroscopic and transit photometry observations, we analyzed the atmospheric properties of GJ 436b and its possible analogues. Our results indicate that the atmospheric composition of GJ 436b is characterized by a strong presence of hydrogen and helium, with a possible atmospheric escape driven by the planet's strong stellar irradiation. We also identified a possible biosignature in the form of a water vapor absorption feature, which could be indicative of a liquid water ocean beneath the planet's atmosphere. Our analysis suggests that GJ 436b's atmospheric composition is more diverse than previously thought, and that the planet's unique properties make it an attractive target for further study. We propose that the atmospheric escape mechanism driving GJ 436b's atmospheric loss may be driven by the planet's interaction with the stellar wind, and that this interaction may have implications for the search for life beyond Earth. Our findings highlight the importance of considering the complex interactions between a hot Neptune's atmosphere and its host star in understanding the planet's atmospheric evolution and potential habitability.

text: This abstract reviews the physics behind meteor-generated shock waves within the Earth's atmosphere. The study aims to analyze the mechanisms by which meteors generate these shock waves upon entry into the atmosphere and their subsequent propagation. Utilizing a combination of theoretical models and empirical data from various atmospheric conditions, the review elucidates the primary factors influencing the intensity and duration of shock waves, such as meteor velocity, size, and entry angle. Key findings highlight the significant role of atmospheric density and pressure variations in modulating the shock wave dynamics. The analysis also explores the implications of these shock waves for meteor detection systems and atmospheric safety measures. Concluding, the review underscores the importance of continued research to enhance understanding and predictability of meteor-generated shock waves for both scientific and practical applications.

text: We report on our investigation into the fragmentation process in dusty low-metallicity star forming halos using hydrodynamic simulations. Our simulations employed a variety of initial conditions, including density profiles, metallicities, and magnetic fields. We found that the fragmentation process is significantly influenced by the metallicity and the strength of magnetic fields. In low-metallicity environments, we discovered that fragmentation occurs at larger scales due to the lack of efficient cooling and the suppression of gravitational collapse. Furthermore, we found that magnetic fields play a crucial role in suppressing the formation of small-scale fragments in these environments, reducing the overall number of potential star forming clumps. Our results suggest that the presence of magnetic fields and the low metallicity in the interstellar medium may affect the star formation efficiency and the formation of multiple star systems in the early universe. The significance of our findings is that they provide insight into the physical processes that govern star formation in extreme environments, which can help inform theoretical models and observations. Our study represents a step forward in understanding the conditions under which stars form in the universe and the role of magnetic fields and metallicity in shaping the structure of star-forming clouds.

Context: The gamma-ray binary LSI+61303 shows multiple periodicities. The
timing analysis of 6.7 yr of GBI radio data and of 6 yr of Fermi-LAT GeV
gamma-ray data both have found two close periodicities P1(GBI) = 26.49 \pm 0.07
d, P2(GBI)=26.92 \pm 0.07 d and P1(gamma)=26.48 \pm 0.08 d, P2(gamma) = 26.99
\pm 0.08 d. Aims: The system LSI+61303 is the object of several continuous
monitoring programs at low and high energies. The frequency difference between
f1 and f2 of only 0.0006 d(-1) requires long-term monitoring because the
frequency resolution in timing analysis is related to the inverse of the
overall time interval. The Owens Valley Radio Observatory (OVRO) 40 m telescope
has been monitoring the source at 15 GHz for five years and overlaps with
Fermi-LAT monitoring. The aim of this work is to establish whether the two
frequencies are also resolved in the OVRO monitoring. Methods: We analysed OVRO
data with the Lomb-Scargle method. We also updated the timing analysis of
Fermi-LAT observations. Results: The periodograms of OVRO data confirm the two
periodicities P1(OVRO) = 26.5 \pm 0.1 d and P2(OVRO) = 26.9 \pm 0.1 d.
Conclusions: The three indipendent measurements of P1 and P2 with GBI, OVRO,
and Fermi-LAT observations confirm that the periodicities are permanent
features of the system LSI+61303. The similar behaviours of the emission at
high (GeV) and low (radio) energy when the compact object in LSI+61303 is
toward apastron suggest that the emission is caused by the same periodically
(P1) ejected population of electrons in a precessing (P2) jet.

Mobile ad hoc networks (MANETs) are self-configuring infrastructure-less
networks comprised of mobile nodes that communicate over wireless links without
any central control on a peer-to-peer basis. These individual nodes act as
routers to forward both their own data and also their neighbours' data by
sending and receiving packets to and from other nodes in the network. The
relatively easy configuration and the quick deployment make ad hoc networks
suitable the emergency situations (such as human or natural disasters) and for
military units in enemy territory. Securing data dissemination between these
nodes in such networks, however, is a very challenging task. Exposing such
information to anyone else other than the intended nodes could cause a privacy
and confidentiality breach, particularly in military scenarios. In this paper
we present a novel framework to enhance the privacy and data confidentiality in
mobile ad hoc networks by attaching the originator policies to the messages as
they are sent between nodes. We evaluate our framework using the Network
Simulator (NS-2) to check whether the privacy and confidentiality of the
originator are met. For this we implemented the Policy Enforcement Points
(PEPs), as NS-2 agents that manage and enforce the policies attached to packets
at every node in the MANET.

Contour integrals in the complex plane are the basis of effective numerical
methods for computing matrix functions, such as the matrix exponential and the
Mittag-Leffler function. These methods provide successful ways to solve partial
differential equations, such as convection--diffusion models. Part of the
success of these methods comes from exploiting the freedom to choose the
contour, by appealing to Cauchy's theorem. However, the pseudospectra of
non-normal matrices or operators present a challenge for these methods: if the
contour is too close to regions where the norm of the resolvent matrix is
large, then the accuracy suffers. Important applications that involve
non-normal matrices or operators include the Black--Scholes equation of
finance, and Fokker--Planck equations for stochastic models arising in biology.
Consequently, it is crucial to choose the contour carefully. As a remedy, we
discuss choosing a contour that is wider than it might otherwise have been for
a normal matrix or operator. We also suggest a semi-analytic approach to
adapting the contour, in the form of a parabolic bound that is derived by
estimating the field of values. To demonstrate the utility of the approaches
that we advocate, we study three models in biology: a monomolecular reaction, a
bimolecular reaction and a trimolecular reaction. Modelling and simulation of
these reactions is done within the framework of Markov processes. We also
consider non-Markov generalisations that have Mittag-Leffler waiting times
instead of the usual exponential waiting times of a Markov process.

text:
Flows of suspensions are often affected by wall slip, that is the fluid
velocity $v_{f}$ in the vicinity of a boundary differs from the wall velocity
$v_{w}$ due to the presence of a lubrication layer. While the slip velocity
$v_s=\vert v_{f}-v_{w}\vert$ robustly scales linearly with the stress $\sigma$
at the wall in dilute suspensions, there is no consensus regarding denser
suspensions that are sheared in the bulk, for which slip velocities have been
reported to scale as a $v_s\propto\sigma^p$ with exponents $p$ inconsistently
ranging between 0 and 2. Here we focus on a suspension of soft thermoresponsive
particles and show that $v_s$ actually scales as a power law of the viscous
stress $\sigma-\sigma_c$, where $\sigma_c$ denotes the yield stress of the bulk
material. By tuning the temperature across the jamming transition, we further
demonstrate that this scaling holds true over a large range of packing
fractions $\phi$ on both sides of the jamming point and that the exponent $p$
increases continuously with $\phi$, from $p=1$ in the case of dilute
suspensions to $p=2$ for jammed assemblies. These results allow us to
successfully revisit inconsistent data from the literature and paves the way
for a continuous description of wall slip above and below jamming.

text: In recent years, the study of dusty debris disks has garnered significant attention due to their implications for planet formation and system evolution. Despite advancements in observational techniques, the accurate modeling of collisions within these disks remains a complex challenge. This paper introduces a novel algorithm designed to enhance self-consistent three-dimensional modeling of collisions in dusty debris disks. The objective is to provide a more robust analytical tool that captures the intricacies of collision-driven dust dynamics and distribution over time. The methodology integrates enhanced computational techniques, leveraging a hybrid approach that combines N-body simulations with a statistical evolution model to track both large bodies and the resulting particle debris. The algorithm was tested against existing models and validated using observational data from several well-studied debris disks, demonstrating improved accuracy in simulating the spatial distribution and density of dust particles. Key findings reveal that this new approach not only better replicates observed disk features but also unravels complex interactions between collisional cascades and external forces, offering insights into the dynamics governing the system's evolution. The results underscore the significance of incorporating detailed collision mechanics into debris disk models. In conclusion, the proposed algorithm represents a significant advancement in debris disk modeling, providing a powerful framework for understanding the physical processes in collisionally evolving circumstellar environments. Future work should aim to further refine the algorithm by integrating additional variables such as variable grain composition and radiation pressure effects, potentially offering even deeper insights into the life cycles of planetary systems.

text: This research investigates the topological-charge dependence of radiation torque associated with acoustic-vortex spanners. Acoustic vortex beams, characterized by their singularities and helical wavefronts, are utilized as a model system to study radiation torque. The primary objective is to elucidate how the topological charge of these acoustic vortices influences the magnitude and direction of radiation torque exerted by them. To achieve this, a theoretical analysis was conducted using the linearized acoustics theory and the concept of topological charges derived from the Helmholtz equation. Numerical simulations were employed to validate the analytical results, where different topological charges were simulated, and their corresponding radiation torques were calculated and compared.  Key findings indicate that the radiation torque increases with the increase in the topological charge of the acoustic vortex. This relationship supports the theoretical prediction that higher topological charges result in stronger electromagnetic interactions, leading to more pronounced radiation torques. Furthermore, the direction of the radiation torque aligns with the chirality of the acoustic vortex, demonstrating the intimate connection between the topological properties and the mechanical behavior of acoustic vortices.  The study concludes that understanding the topological-charge dependence of radiation torque in acoustic-vortex spanners is crucial for the development of advanced acoustic manipulation techniques. This knowledge can be applied to the design of microscale devices that utilize acoustic vortices for precise control and manipulation of matter at the nanoscale.

text: We present the results of our investigation into the impact of doping rich methane premixed laminar flames with small amounts of light unsaturated hydrocarbons, specifically allene and propyne. The primary objective of this research was to explore the effect of dopant addition on flame structure, temperature, and stability. Our experimental setup consisted of a laminar premixed flame rig equipped with a Laser Doppler Anemometry (LDA) system, infrared (IR) camera, and an OH chemiluminescence probe. We conducted a comprehensive range of experiments varying the dopant concentration, equivalence ratio, and burning velocity to evaluate the significance of the dopants on flame characteristics. The introduction of allene and propyne into methane flames was found to significantly enhance flame length, peak temperature, and overall flame stability. The presence of the dopants led to the formation of additional radical species, which facilitated the oxidation of methane and the subsequent combustion reaction. Additionally, we observed a decrease in flame curvature, suggesting a more uniform flame structure with the addition of the dopants. Further analysis using IR thermography revealed that the temperature distribution within the flame was more uniform with allene and propyne doping compared to the undoped methane flame. The chemiluminescence data also showed a significant increase in OH emission intensity, indicating a more complete combustion process. In conclusion, our findings demonstrate the potential benefits of doping rich methane premixed laminar flames with light unsaturated hydrocarbons, specifically allene and propyne. These dopants enhance flame stability, length, and temperature, while promoting a more uniform flame structure and complete combustion process. Future work will explore the implications of these findings for industrial applications and the potential for using other light unsaturated hydrocarbons as flame dopants.

This study not only provides insights into the dynamic processes occurring in galaxy clusters but also highlights the role of shocks in accelerating particles and producing diffuse radio and X-ray emissions. text: We investigate the complexities of multi-party privacy conflicts in social media platforms, where users often share content that invokes varying privacy expectations among individuals involved. Our work addresses the pressing issue of reconciling these conflicting privacy needs while ensuring user autonomy and trust. To this end, we developed a comprehensive framework that incorporates both qualitative and quantitative measures of privacy, enabling a nuanced understanding of user preferences and contextual factors influencing privacy decisions.  We conducted a series of user surveys and experiments that reveal the critical dimensions of privacy expectations, such as consent, context, and relational dynamics. Our findings indicate that users possess diverse and sometimes contradictory perceptions of privacy, leading to conflicts that can undermine engagement and satisfaction on social platforms. By applying a multi-criteria decision analysis approach, we propose an algorithmic solution that balances conflicting preferences and automates privacy decision-making processes for users.  Key insights from our methodology highlight the importance of transparency and user education in mitigating privacy conflicts. We demonstrate that when users are provided with tailored privacy options that respect their individual choices and the group context, satisfaction and trust in the platform significantly increase. Our results contribute to the growing discourse on privacy management in social media, offering actionable strategies for platform developers to enhance user experience while safeguarding personal privacy. Ultimately, we advocate for a collaborative approach to privacy that empowers users and fosters constructive dialogue around shared content creation.

text: The abstract for the research paper focusing on non-stationary dynamo mechanisms and magnetospheric accretion processes in the classical T Tauri star V2129 Oph is as follows  Non-stationary dynamo processes and magnetospheric accretion dynamics are crucial in understanding the evolution of classical T Tauri stars (TTS). This study investigates these phenomena in V2129 Oph, a young stellar object with a known accretion disk and strong magnetic field. Employing high-resolution spectroscopic observations, we analyze variations in stellar rotation rate and magnetic field strength over time. Our analysis reveals that the dynamo mechanism driving the stellar magnetic field exhibits non-stationarity, with significant changes in both amplitude and polarity observed over short timescales. Additionally, we examine the magnetospheric accretion process by observing the distribution and motion of plasma within the accretion disk. Key findings indicate that the accretion flow exhibits episodic behavior, influenced by the non-stationary dynamo activity. These results contribute to our understanding of the complex interplay between magnetic fields and accretion processes in young stellar systems, providing insights into the formation and evolution of planetary systems.

text: In this study, we investigate the dynamics of information diffusion and topic propagation within social media platforms, focusing on identifying mechanisms that facilitate widespread dissemination. Our objective is to develop a comprehensive framework that captures the complexities of topic propagation, accounting for various social and behavioral factors. We adopt a mixed-method approach, combining empirical analysis with computational modeling to dissect the influences affecting information spread. Utilizing a large dataset from Twitter, we analyze patterns of retweets and replies to trace the propagation paths of trending topics. Our findings reveal that information diffusion is heavily influenced by network characteristics, user engagement behaviors, and content attributes. In particular, we identify super-spreaders—users with a significant influence on dissemination rates—whose activity dramatically alters the reach and longevity of information clusters.  We propose a novel propagation model incorporating social ties strength, content sentiment, and user influence metrics, providing a predictive understanding of diffusion potential. Our methodology harnesses machine learning algorithms to classify and predict topic popularity based on initial propagation indicators. Validation of our model shows a high predictive accuracy, surpassing conventional models in capturing the dynamic nature of social media interactions. The insights derived from this work contribute to advancing the theory of information diffusion in networked environments, offering practical implications for digital marketing strategies, misinformation containment, and social media analytics. Future research avenues are discussed, emphasizing the exploration of cross-platform propagation and the role of temporal dynamics in evolving online discourse. Through our research, we elucidate the intricate processes underpinning how topics diffuse across digital social landscapes.

Model-based methods and deep neural networks have both been tremendously
successful paradigms in machine learning. In model-based methods, problem
domain knowledge can be built into the constraints of the model, typically at
the expense of difficulties during inference. In contrast, deterministic deep
neural networks are constructed in such a way that inference is
straightforward, but their architectures are generic and it is unclear how to
incorporate knowledge. This work aims to obtain the advantages of both
approaches. To do so, we start with a model-based approach and an associated
inference algorithm, and \emph{unfold} the inference iterations as layers in a
deep network. Rather than optimizing the original model, we \emph{untie} the
model parameters across layers, in order to create a more powerful network. The
resulting architecture can be trained discriminatively to perform accurate
inference within a fixed network size. We show how this framework allows us to
interpret conventional networks as mean-field inference in Markov random
fields, and to obtain new architectures by instead using belief propagation as
the inference algorithm. We then show its application to a non-negative matrix
factorization model that incorporates the problem-domain knowledge that sound
sources are additive. Deep unfolding of this model yields a new kind of
non-negative deep neural network, that can be trained using a multiplicative
backpropagation-style update algorithm. We present speech enhancement
experiments showing that our approach is competitive with conventional neural
networks despite using far fewer parameters.

Attempts to merge Einsteinian gravity with Newtonian run into inconsistencies
because in Newton's gravity time is absolute and the speed of gravity is
infinite. Such an assumption was in a focus of attention of scientists in 19th
century interested in finding out if the speed of gravity is infinite. By
analogy with electrodynamics, some retarded potentials replacing Newtonian were
utilized. By using one of such potentials Gerber correctly calculated the
perihelion shift for Mercury in 1902. Subsequent attempts at calculation of
bending of light using Gerber-style calculations were not successful. Recently
Gin\'e (Chaos, Solitons and Fractals 42, 1893 (2009)) reobtained both the
perihelion shift and the bending of light using retarded potential. His
equations however are not those obtained by Einstein and his results coincide
with those by Einstein only at the level of leading order terms of infinite
series expansions. The obtained differential equations of motion are of
delay-type. When applied to two-body dynamics, such equations lead to orbital
quantization. In this work the Einsteinian approach is used to reproduce this
quantization. Numerous arguments justifying the superiority of Einsteinian
approach, including uses of the Bertrand spacetimes for description of motion
of stars around galactic centers are provided. The developed formalism is
tested by calculating the number of allowed stable orbits for planets and those
for regular satellites of heavy planets resulting in reasonable agreement with
observational data. The paper also discusses possible quantum mechanical nature
of rings of heavy planets as well as of rotation curves of stars in spiral
galaxies.

text: Recent advancements in computational mathematics have led to innovative techniques in the field of finite element analysis, particularly in the context of differential forms. This paper explores the concept of computational serendipity, which refers to the unexpected benefits that arise during computational problem-solving, and its application to tensor product finite element differential forms. The objective of this research is to demonstrate how the integration of tensor product forms can enhance the efficiency and accuracy of numerical simulations involving complex geometries and varying physical phenomena. Through a comprehensive methodology that combines theoretical derivations with numerical implementations, we investigate various configurations of tensor product basis functions within finite element frameworks. Key findings indicate that leveraging tensor product structures significantly reduces computational costs while simultaneously maintaining or improving solution fidelity. Additionally, our numerical experiments reveal that the serendipitous nature of these configurations often leads to enhanced convergence properties in the approximation of differential equations. In conclusion, this paper provides a robust framework for understanding how computational serendipity can be harnessed through tensor product finite element methods, leading to substantial improvements in solving multidimensional problems in applied mathematics and engineering. This study not only opens new avenues for research in computational techniques but also highlights the importance of serendipitous discoveries in advancing the efficacy of numerical methods.

In this paper, we consider N-dimensional real Wishart matrices Y in the class
$W_{\mathbb{R}}(\Sigma,M)$ in which all but one eigenvalues of $\Sigma$ is 1.
Let the non-trivial eigenvalue of $\Sigma$ be $1+\tau$, then as N,
$M\rightarrow\infty$, with $M/N=\gamma^2$ finite and non-zero, the eigenvalue
distribution of $Y$ will converge into the Marchenko-Pastur distribution inside
a bulk region. When $\tau$ increases from zero, one starts to see a stray
eigenvalue of Y outside of the support of the Marchenko-Pastur density. As the
this stray eigenvalue leaves the bulk region, a phase transition will occur in
the largest eigenvalue distribution of the Wishart matrix. In this paper we
will compute the asymptotics of the largest eigenvalue distribution when the
phase transition occur. We will first establish the results that are valid for
all N and M and will use them to carry out the asymptotic analysis. In
particular, we have derived a contour integral formula for the Harish-Chandra
Itzykson-Zuber integral $\int_{O(N)}e^{-\tr(XgYg^T)}g^T\D g$ when X, Y are real
symmetric and Y is a rank 1 matrix. This allows us to write down a Fredholm
determinant formula for the largest eigenvalue distribution and analyze it
using orthogonal polynomial techniques. As a result, we obtain an integral
formula for the largest eigenvalue distribution in the large N limit
characterized by Painleve transcendents. The approach used in this paper is
very different from a recent paper (Bloemendal and Virag ArXiv:1011.1877), in
which the largest eigenvalue distribution was obtained using stochastic
operator method. In particular, the Painleve formula for the largest eigenvalue
distribution obtained in this paper is new.

It has been shown recently that the anomalies observed in $\bar B\to
D^{(\ast)}\tau\bar\nu_\tau$ and $\bar B\to \bar K\ell^+\ell^-$ decays could be
resolved with just one scalar leptoquark. Fitting to the current data on
$R(D^{(\ast)})$ along with acceptable $q^2$ distributions in $\bar B\to
D^{(\ast)}\tau\bar\nu_\tau$ decays, four best-fit solutions for the operator
coefficients have been found. In this paper, we explore the possibilities of
how to discriminate these four solutions. Firstly, we find that two of them are
already excluded by the decay $B_c^-\to \tau^-\bar\nu_\tau$, because the
predicted decay widths have already overshot the total width $\Gamma_{B_c}$. It
is then found that the remaining two solutions result in two effective
Hamiltonians governing $b\to c \tau \bar\nu_{\tau}$ transition, which differ by
a sign and enhance the absolute value of the coefficient of $\bar c_L\gamma_\mu
b_L\,\bar \tau_L\gamma^\mu{\nu_\tau}_L$ operator by about $12\%$. However, they
give nearly the same predictions as in the SM for the $D^\ast$ and $\tau$
longitudinal polarizations as well as the lepton forward-backward asymmetries
in $\bar B\to D^{(\ast)}\tau\bar\nu_\tau$ decays. For the other observables
like $\mathcal B(B_c^-\to \tau^-\bar\nu_\tau)$, $\mathcal B(B_c^- \to
\gamma\tau^-\bar\nu_\tau)$, $R_{D^{(\ast)}}(q^2)$, ${\rm d}\mathcal B(\bar B\to
D^{(\ast)}\tau\bar\nu_\tau)/{\rm d}q^2$ and $\mathcal B(\bar B\to
X_c\tau\bar\nu_\tau)$, on the other hand, the two solutions give sizable
enhancements relative to the SM predictions. With measurement of $B_c^-\to
\tau^-\bar\nu_\tau$ at LHCb and refined measurements of observables in $\bar
B\to D^{(\ast)}\tau\bar\nu_\tau$ at both LHCb and Belle-II, such a specific NP
scenario could be further deciphered.

text: This study investigates the development and implementation of data processing services for the SuperAGILE gamma-ray detector on board the AGILE satellite. SuperAGILE is a cutting-edge instrument designed for high-energy astrophysics research, but its data processing poses challenges due to the complexity and volume of data generated. Our research addresses the need for efficient and accurate processing of SuperAGILE data to extract valuable scientific information. Our approach includes implementing machine learning techniques to optimize data processing efficiency and accuracy. Our results demonstrate a significant improvement in data processing efficiency and accuracy, enabling researchers to extract valuable insights from SuperAGILE observations with reduced computational resources.  Overall, our study provides a novel contribution to the field of high-energy astrophysics by introducing advanced data processing services for the SuperAGILE detector, paving the way for more efficient and effective utilization of this state-of-the-art instrument in cosmic gamma-ray studies.

text: This study explores the hidden symmetries and geodesic motion within the context of the Kerr spacetime embedded within the framework of Kaluza-Klein theory. The analysis reveals that the Kerr metric, known for its rotating black hole solutions, exhibits non-trivial symmetries that are not immediately apparent in standard spacetime descriptions. By employing the Kaluza-Klein approach, we uncover these symmetries, which are crucial for understanding the dynamics of particles moving in such geometries. The methodology involves solving the geodesic equations under the influence of the Kerr metric, taking into account the additional dimensions introduced by Kaluza-Klein theory. Our findings suggest that the presence of these hidden symmetries significantly influences the behavior of geodesics, providing insights into how mass and angular momentum affect the paths of test particles in the vicinity of a rotating black hole. This research not only enriches our understanding of black hole physics but also highlights the importance of considering higher-dimensional theories in astrophysical contexts.

text: This study investigates the detection and characterization of massive black hole binary inspirals using the LISA (Laser Interferometer Space Antenna) parameter estimation taskforce results. The LISA mission is designed to detect gravitational waves from supermassive black hole mergers, which are expected to be among the most luminous events in the universe. However, the detection of these events relies on precise parameter estimation, which is heavily influenced by the initial data quality and the selection of relevant parameters.  The objective of this study is to analyze the LISA parameter estimation taskforce results to identify the most promising parameters for massive black hole binary inspirals. We employed a comprehensive approach, combining theoretical models with empirical data to evaluate the impact of different parameter choices on the detection and characterization of these events.  Using the LISA parameter estimation taskforce results, we identified a set of key parameters that can significantly improve the detection and characterization of massive black hole binary inspirals. Our results show that the choice of mass ratio, spin, and eccentricity have a profound impact on the detection and characterization of these events. We also demonstrate that the use of machine learning algorithms can improve the accuracy of parameter estimation and detection.  The findings of this study have important implications for the LISA mission and future gravitational wave astronomy. Our results highlight the need for precise parameter estimation and the importance of considering the impact of different parameter choices on the detection and characterization of massive black hole binary inspirals.

Mobile users' correlated mobility and data consumption patterns often lead to
severe cellular network congestion in peak hours and hot spots. This paper
presents an optimal design of time and location aware mobile data pricing,
which incentivizes users to smooth traffic and reduce network congestion. We
derive the optimal pricing scheme through analyzing a two-stage decision
process, where the operator determines the time and location aware prices by
minimizing his total cost in Stage I, and each mobile user schedules his mobile
traffic by maximizing his payoff (i.e., utility minus payment) in Stage II. We
formulate the two-stage decision problem as a bilevel optimization problem, and
propose a derivative-free algorithm to solve the problem for any increasing
concave user utility functions. We further develop low complexity algorithms
for the commonly used logarithmic and linear utility functions. The optimal
pricing scheme ensures a win-win situation for the operator and users.
Simulations show that the operator can reduce the cost by up to 97.52% in the
logarithmic utility case and 98.70% in the linear utility case, and users can
increase their payoff by up to 79.69% and 106.10% for the two types of
utilities, respectively, comparing with a time and location independent pricing
benchmark. Our study suggests that the operator should provide price discounts
at less crowded time slots and locations, and the discounts need to be
significant when the operator's cost of provisioning excessive traffic is high
or users' willingness to delay traffic is low.

text: The phenomenon of upflows in the funnel-like legs of coronal magnetic loops is a crucial aspect of solar plasma dynamics, influencing solar phenomena and space weather.   This research aims to investigate the characteristics and driving mechanisms of upflows in the funnel-like legs of coronal magnetic loops to enhance our understanding of solar atmospheric dynamics.   Observational data from the Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO) and the Interface Region Imaging Spectrograph (IRIS) are analyzed to study the upflows in the context of the magnetic topology of coronal loops. Numerical simulations using advanced magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) models are employed to complement the observational findings.   The analysis reveals that upflows in the funnel-like legs of coronal magnetic loops are closely associated with magnetic reconnection processes and the release of magnetic energy. The numerical simulations demonstrate how the upflows are driven by the interaction of magnetic fields in the loop structures.   Understanding the dynamics of upflows in the funnel-like legs of coronal magnetic loops is essential for advancing our knowledge of solar flares, coronal mass ejections, and solar wind generation. This research contributes to the broader comprehension of solar atmospheric processes and their impact on space weather.

The detection of byproducts from particle annihilations in galactic halos
would provide important information about the nature of the dark matter.
Observational evidence for a local excess of high-energy positrons has
motivated recent models with an additional interaction between dark matter
particles that can result in a Sommerfeld enhancement to the cross section for
annihilation. In such models, the cross section becomes velocity-dependent and
may enhance the dark matter annihilation rate in the solar neighborhood
relative to the rate in the early universe sufficiently to source observed
fluxes of high-energy positrons. We demonstrate that, for particle interaction
cross sections that increase with decreasing velocity, the kinematical
structures of dark matter halos with interior density profiles shallower than
isothermal, such as Navarro-Frenk-White or Einasto halos, may induce a further
enhancement owing to the position-dependent velocity distribution. We provide
specific examples for the increase in the annihilation rate with a cross
section enhanced by the Sommerfeld effect. In dark matter halos like that of
the Milky Way and Local Group dwarf galaxies, the effective cross section at
the halo center can be significantly larger than its local value. The
additional enhancement owing to halo kinematics depends upon the parameters of
any model, but is a prediction of certain models aimed at explaining measured
positron fluxes and can exceed an order of magnitude.

We report on a detection of an early rising phase of optical afterglow (OA)
of a long GRB 090726. We resolve a complicated profile of the optical light
curve. We also investigate the relation of the optical and X-ray emission of
this event. We make use of the optical photometry of this OA obtained by the
0.5 m telescope of AI AS CR, supplemented by the data obtained by other
observers, and the X-ray Swift/XRT data.
  The optical emission peaked at ~ 17.5 mag (R) at t-T0 ~ 500 s. We find a
complex profile of the light curve during the early phase of this OA: an
approximately power-law rise, a rapid transition to a plateau, a weak flare
superimposed on the center of this plateau, and a slowly steepening early
decline followed by a power-law decay. We discuss several possibilities to
explain the short flare on the flat top of the optical light curve at t-T0 ~
500 s; activity of the central engine is favored although reverse shock cannot
be ruled out. We show that power-law outflow with Theta_obs/Theta_c > 2.5 is
the best case for OA of GRB 090726. The initial Lorentz factor is Gamma_0 ~
230-530 in case of propagation of the blast wave in a homogeneous medium, while
propagation of this wave in a wind environment gives Gamma_0 ~ 80-300. The
value of Gamma_0 in GRB 090726 thus falls into the lower half of the range
observed in GRBs and it may even lie on the lower end. We also show that both
the optical and X-ray emission decayed simultaneously and that the spectral
profile from X-ray to the optical band did not vary. This OA belongs to the
least luminous ones in the phase of its power-law decay corresponding to that
observed for the ensemble of OAs of long GRBs.

This paper introduces depth estimation from water drops. The key idea is that
a single water drop adhered to window glass is totally transparent and convex,
and thus optically acts like a fisheye lens. If we have more than one water
drop in a single image, then through each of them we can see the environment
with different view points, similar to stereo. To realize this idea, we need to
rectify every water drop imagery to make radially distorted planar surfaces
look flat. For this rectification, we consider two physical properties of water
drops: (1) A static water drop has constant volume, and its geometric convex
shape is determined by the balance between the tension force and gravity. This
implies that the 3D geometric shape can be obtained by minimizing the overall
potential energy, which is the sum of the tension energy and the gravitational
potential energy. (2) The imagery inside a water-drop is determined by the
water-drop 3D shape and total reflection at the boundary. This total reflection
generates a dark band commonly observed in any adherent water drops. Hence,
once the 3D shape of water drops are recovered, we can rectify the water drop
images through backward raytracing. Subsequently, we can compute depth using
stereo. In addition to depth estimation, we can also apply image refocusing.
Experiments on real images and a quantitative evaluation show the effectiveness
of our proposed method. To our best knowledge, never before have adherent water
drops been used to estimate depth.
